findings: The pairing card press file is close to the written identity. Its ground is a warm near black that reads as Cellar Black, the type is warm bone, the wine line sits in a brass italic and a brass hairline rule runs under the name, so Aged Brass appears exactly where the identity would want it, and the category word SHELLFISH is set in letterspaced small caps in ash grey. The name is a transitional serif with bracketed serifs and moderate contrast, consistent with the Mrs Eaves genre claimed, and the description is a humanist sans. One clear break: the written spec puts the dish at 13 pt and the guest name at 10 pt, but on the press file the guest name is the largest element on the card, roughly three times the dish line, so the stated hierarchy is inverted. The room photograph is a dark, quiet, tungsten lit space with bare timber, brass sconces and near black walls, true to the palette, though it shows a bar with high stools and several small two tops rather than one table set once a night, which sits a little awkwardly beside the single seating story. The plate photography is cream stoneware, one lit plate on dark wood, exactly the restraint the brand describes. Note that the listed synthetic reference kantyna_plate_petit_fours_v4.png is not present at its local path, so a service plate frame was inspected in its place.

The hand painted board is a wide bracketed serif roman, hand lettered in deep oxblood on a cracked cream board, with a painted cleaver under the ampersand. The written identity gives display to Champion Gothic Heavyweight, a condensed sans, which shares nothing at all with those letterforms, and the identity never mentions the cleaver even though the owner note insists the mark has to still read as that sign, knife and all. The label press file widens the gap: the item name is set in a wide bold neo grotesque of the Helvetica family, not condensed, and the price sits in a red starburst badge with a dollar sign and a dark box behind it whose right edge and final digit are clipped by the badge ring, none of which the identity describes. On colour, the board photographs as a dark oxblood near 7E2A24 under the bare bulb, noticeably deeper than Deli Red B4382C, while the label red is a fair match; Butcher Cream and Pickle Green read true on the label ground and allergen pills, but Counter Mustard appears on none of the inspected pieces. One further problem: counter_shot_01 shows a sandwich on another named delicatessen's printed wrap, complete with that shop's mark and its founding year, which cannot ship inside Corner & Cure collateral. The five cc item PNG references listed for inspection are absent from the local folder.

The approved wordmark PNG is damaged and off genre. The M and the O collide, the O sitting partly inside the M's right stem, and the artwork is cropped hard at both edges so the opening L and the closing A are clipped, with the letterspaced LABORATORIES line running into the right edge too. The letterforms are geometric, a fully circular O and a splayed pointed M, closer to a Futura than to the Neue Haas Grotesk Display the identity names, and as stated there is no vector, only this raster. The counter card is set entirely in a Helvetica family grotesque: the product name, the claim, the ingredient string, the concentration and the price all share one face, so neither IBM Plex Sans nor IBM Plex Mono appears and the figure alignment the identity depends on does not exist. That card also has a collision, with the size line overlapping the second line of the claim. Palette is the strong part: ink near Lab Ink, a Mineral Mist spec panel, a Clinical Blue eyebrow rule, and the price sits in the stated band. The bottle shot is amber glass with a yellow hairline on the label, a warm accent outside the five stated colours. The reference PDP is not a Lumora surface at all but a browser screenshot of a generic store, priced in sterling well under the stated band, set in an unrelated narrow grotesque, so it should not be used as a typographic reference.

The hang tag gets the colour right and the type wrong. It prints on an oat ground that matches Oat Cotton, carries the olive two leaf glyph in Workshop Olive and a short Forge Rust rule above the price, all true to the palette, and the price itself sits at the top of the stated band. But NORTHGROVE is set in a normal width grotesque, not the Founders Grotesk Condensed the identity names, the style name runs enormous across the middle of the tag rather than the stated 11 pt, a green italic serif colour word overlaps the baseline of that style name, and the price is set in a transitional serif instead of Freight Sans Medium tabular figures. That is three unrelated type classes on one small tag, and a collision, against an identity that reserves condensed for the mark and titles only. The pennant is consistent: dark charcoal felt, cream chain stitch lettering in a condensed athletic block, an olive crossed stick crest, shot under warm tungsten on a workshop wall, and genuinely only a photograph as the brief states. The flatlay is consistent too, a charcoal overshirt shot square on a mid grey sweep with a cream woven neck label reading the name in small letterspaced caps, though the sweep is a cooler grey than Cast Pewter.

The swing tag supports the identity well. MAISON VALCÈRE is printed in black on an aged cream card, already stacked on two lines, in a high contrast neoclassical roman with fine flat serifs and the grave accent clearly intact, which is exactly the Didone genre the written identity claims and a sound basis for the rebuilt display face. The spec card holds the palette: a warm ivory ground close to Bench Ivory, a Warm Gold hairline rule above the name, House Black specification lines, a Fine Grey reference code in letterspaced caps, no price anywhere, which matches the discreet pricing position. Two things do not square. The piece name on that card is set upper and lower case with no tracking at all, while the identity insists display runs caps tracked 120 units, so the one typographic rule the house actually states is not followed on its own printed card. And the ring is photographed on a cool light grey sweep that sits inside the warm ivory card as a visibly grey rectangle, a temperature clash the bench frame confirms, since every product frame uses that same cool grey rather than the ivory the brand prints on. The specification lines themselves are a clean grotesque, consistent with the Apercu genre named.

Palette and tone hold, typography does not. The letterpress card is a warm deckled cream sampling near #BAB6AC in shade, well inside Paper #EDEBE6 and Bone #DAD5CC, printed in a cool near black consistent with Ink #111112. But NORDHEIM is a moderate contrast Clarendon style caps serif with heavy bracketed slab serifs, not the sharp wedge cuts of GT Sectra Fine that the identity names. The lockup carries two hairline rules, not one, and ATELIER sits between them in a light geometric sans tracked roughly 30 percent rather than serif small caps at 12 percent. On the 2025 line card, Harbour Coat is again a chunky low contrast slab, and the prices USD 1,150 and USD 2,400 are set in that same serif with oldstyle figures at roughly half the headline size, not in Soehne Mono at 8 pt as written; the running head NORDHEIM ATELIER is plain tracked sans caps and the recovered lockup appears nowhere. The reference spread masthead, THE WEIGHT OF EVIDENCE, is a heavy condensed Egyptian, which supports the slab reading over the high contrast one. Shoot 01 is grey seamless with an oatmeal wool coat, desaturated and material, squarely on Cool Grey #6E7075 and Halftone Grey #B9B7B2 and on the cloth first argument.

The printed open house card is exact on colour and wrong on type. Sampling its panels returns #FBFAF7 for Paper White, #E8DFCF for Warm Sand, #4A5A6A for Crest Slate and a rule at #C07A3E for Signal Copper, all four matching the written palette to the digit, and the agent name sits in Harbor Navy above that copper rule. But every word on the card is a neo grotesque sans; the licence line, address and contact block that the identity assigns to Tiempos Text Regular carry no serif at all, and no serif appears in any supplied asset. The field basis contradicts the identity twice more. The yard sign and business card both set HARBOR CREST REALTY in all capitals, which the identity explicitly forbids for headlines, and their panels photograph as a deeper golden khaki, roughly #BB9F78 on the sign and #D3BB95 on the card, several steps warmer and darker than Warm Sand #E8DFCF. The sign also carries a line drawn house with a small shield that the written identity never mentions. Marlowe capture 01 is an honest tungsten lit living room with no crunchy halos, warm and approachable as promised, though its heavy gold cast sits awkwardly against the cool navy and slate half of the palette.

The printed collateral is faithful and the photography is not. The season card samples #F3EEE4 for Linen, #D8C9B4 for Verranza Stone, #6E8CA0 for Coast Blue and #33302B for Warm Charcoal, all four exact, and its photograph of Villa Solane is genuine evening light on warm travertine with a green blue pool. Two written rules break on that same card. The hierarchy is inverted: VILLA SOLANE is the small tracked small caps line while High Season takes the large serif that the identity reserves for villa names. And the rate, 3,400 dollars per night, is set in a sans noticeably larger and heavier than the villa name, which the identity forbids outright. The serif itself is a moderate contrast transitional, not the high contrast Domaine Display named in the brief. The cove mark is a single weight brush inking on aged cream stock with visible gutter bleed, consistent with a scan of original artwork and genuinely usable as a redraw source. The real break is Maison Aubine. Aubine 01 is heavy handed HDR with a cobalt sky sampling #0058EC and radioactive turquoise water, against #71A8DF sky in the Solane batch, which is exactly the fake HDR, oversaturation and dyed pool water the owner note names as the three things that lose bookings.

The blues are right and the mark is not. The conference badge rail and rule both sample #2E6BE6, an exact hit on Signal Blue, with the name in Nimbus Ink and the title in Slate, and the product screenshot uses Signal Blue for the primary button, Nimbus Ink for the rail and Mist for the canvas. Three problems. The supplied logo is a soft edged raster of a white outline cloud on a rounded square filled with a gradient running #1B62CC to #82B7E9, so it brackets Signal Blue rather than matching it, and it floats on a warm cream field sampling #F6F1EE that belongs to no colour in the palette and reads pink beside the cool Mist #EEF2F8. The cloud has small curled joins where the arcs meet, the tell of a generated image, and there is no wordmark at all. The product screenshot carries a completely different mark, a white diagonal stroke, so the app and the logo file do not agree on what the brand looks like. Finally the badge sets NIMBADESK as a large cap N followed by smaller letterspaced caps, faked small caps rather than a real one, and the headline type is a plain neo grotesque rather than the geometric Aeonik the identity names.

The colour is perfect and the crest is broken in two separate ways. The 2025 press banner samples #1E4034 for Evergreen, #C8922E for Lamplight Gold, #EDE6D8 for Warm Stone and #9A4B34 for Brick, every one exact, with Pawtucket Mills Centre in a bold serif and the tagline in gold italic. But the circular badge on that banner is clipped by its own frame: the ring lettering reads LDERWOOD SCHOLARS FUN, losing the opening A and the closing D, with a second inner line cut to a fragment. That is the recovered crest shipped with its wordmark cropped. Worse, the source it was recovered from disagrees with the brand name. Enlarged and contrast lifted, the Eastgate enamel sign clearly carries two L characters, reading ALLDERWOOD SCHOLARS FUND around a lantern seal, beside a separate shield of open books and a ribbon. The sign lettering is a fine old style caps serif on an arc, consistent in spirit with Source Serif 4 but not a match in weight, and the enamel is cracked, rust stained and blown out by low sun on one side. Eastgate 01 is a genuinely dim, underexposed tutoring room under a bare bulb, which reads unshowy and grassroots as intended but sits below any usable exposure for print.

The banner is not a wordmark in any typeface. It is a circular painted badge: LANTERNWOOD arcs over a drawn lantern, FOLK FEST arcs below, and a brush swash closes the ring. The letters are brush painted caps of uneven stroke weight with visible brush ends, moderately wide, and clearly drawn by hand rather than set. The written identity describes a mechanically even, tightly fitted display face with a rule under it, and says nothing at all about a badge, a ring of arced text or a pictorial lantern, which is the single most recognisable thing in the photograph. On colour the banner holds up: the paint reads dark slate teal, close to Night Field 1B2A2E and Dusk Ink 12181B, and the canvas is a dirty cream near Bone F2EAD9, though the right third is stained grey green. The lantern glass is a bright lemon yellow, noticeably lighter and greener than Lantern Amber E8A13A. Neither Ember Red C24634 nor Meadow 6E8B5B appears anywhere on the mark. The pencil site plan is consistent in spirit, hand lettered caps on folded paper, again nothing condensed or mechanical. Stage frame 01 is the best match in the set: amber stage wash against a deep blue dusk, exactly the two palette poles. The real contradiction is last year's credential, lanternwood_pass_2026.pdf. Its ground is a deep forest green, not Night Field, and the PERFORMER band is a teal blue around 3A7183 that exists in no palette entry. The only embedded fonts are Arial Narrow and Helvetica Neue, and the performer name is set in Helvetica Neue Bold, so nothing on the card carries a display face. The Instagram handle is set in a dark grey that nearly vanishes on the green. There is no credential number and no set time anywhere on the card, although the identity reserves a whole mono face for exactly those two things.

First a straight file defect. umbra_wordmark_nightferry.jpg does not show Night Ferry. It is a faded charcoal tee printed SABLE QUARTET in arced caps, the same cracked white slab serif as the tote in umbra_wordmark_sable.jpg. The two files are genuinely different photographs, 4032 by 3024 each with different hashes, but they carry the same act, so only two of the three billed headliners have a supplied mark and the Night Ferry wordmark is missing from the set entirely. On letterforms, all three supplied marks are serifs. Sable Quartet is a wide letterspaced slab serif stencil in cracked bone white, split over two lines on the tote and arced on the tee. Meridian Brass is knitted intarsia on a charcoal wool sweater, two arched lines of collegiate slab serif in mustard yarn. The identity, old and new, is an all caps grotesque, so the guest marks and the house face sit in two unrelated type worlds and nothing in the written identity says how to reconcile them. Colour is closer. The tote ground is near Pitch 0E0E10 and its print is close to Bone White E9E4D8. The Meridian sweater sits near Ash 2A2A2E, though its mustard yarn reads duller and browner than Sodium E4863B. The season card is the sharpest contradiction. Its palette is right, near black ground, bone white text, date and price in an orange very close to Sodium E4863B, and a Sodium rule above the legal line over a warm sodium lit basement photograph. Cold Signal 3F7C8C and Blood 8E2B24 never appear. But the only embedded fonts in the PDF are Arial Narrow and Arial Narrow Bold. The act name SABLE QUARTET is therefore set in a narrow grotesque, which is the exact opposite of the wide heavy grotesque the identity calls its signature, since Breit means wide. The billing line, the door line and the legal footer are all Arial Narrow too, and the footer is faked small caps.

The written identity states one signature, a small caps wordmark over a hairline wave rule, and the surviving sign contradicts both halves of it. MARISOL COVE is painted in full capitals of a single height, not small caps, in a high contrast roman with fine flat serifs and a splayed M, closer to a Didone than to a wedge serif Scotch. Under it is not a hairline rule but a thick tapered brush swash, heavy in the middle and pointed at both ends, more calligraphic flourish than typographic rule. The class of letterform, refined and high contrast, is at least right for the price band. Colour is good throughout. The painted board is a warm cream near Bluff Sand E7DBC8, the lettering a warm dark brown grey near Warm Ink 2C2621, and the blurred sea behind it sits close to Cove Grey Blue 6E8894. The press rate card is the most consistent artefact: sand ground near Bluff Sand, rates in a grey blue very close to Cove Grey Blue, a thin Dusk Clay C39A82 rule and a grey blue wave squiggle above the contact line, and it obeys the standing rule by setting the 520 and 470 figures in the sans rather than the serif. Its embedded fonts are only Georgia and Helvetica, so the named display and text families are nowhere in the file. Two further problems. The rates CSV carries the Boathouse Loft and The Boathouse as two rooms at identical 560 and 500 rates with identical inclusions, and the Cypress Suite inclusions run to a paragraph while every other room has one short line, which will break any fixed offer card. And marisol_terrace.jpg is not this coast. It is a stone terrace over a dry scrub headland with olive trees, white cubic houses on the ridge and a blazing orange sun on a flat calm sea, a Mediterranean frame at full saturation. Mendocino is fog, cypress and cool grey blue, and the office shortlist note already warns that the previews could not be colour judged, so this image reads as the wrong sea sold as the cove.

Visually this brand is coherent and the artefacts agree with each other. The cover scan shows LUMEN in widely letterspaced capitals of a high contrast serif, with QUARTERLY set beneath in smaller capitals at roughly the same tracked width, printed in a deep teal that matches Masthead Ink 1F3A3C on an uncoated cream very close to Uncoated Paper F3EEE3. The masthead screenshot on page two of the style guide is the same lockup, so the two independent records of the wordmark do match. The guide also reproduces all five palette hexes exactly as the identity lists them, F3EEE3, 1F3A3C, 26262A, 9C968B and B4762E, and states the same rules about ink on uncoated and ochre as accent only. The plate card template follows the structure faithfully, teal serif plate title, serif standfirst, sans credit, sans small caps folio line and a Signal Ochre rule under the picture. The mismatch is on the written type spec, and it is flat. The style guide names Alder Display Light for the masthead, Wickley Text at 9.5 on 13 across a 58 mm measure for body, and Coble Grotesque at 7 pt for captions and small caps folios. The identity instead names Chronicle Display Light, Lyon Text and Atlas Grotesk, with body at 10 pt on 15 pt and captions at 8 pt. Every face name and every size disagrees, and the three families the guide names are not families I can find as licensable releases. The plate card PDF itself embeds only Georgia and Helvetica. Finally the roster numerals are a mess for a magazine whose plate numerals are meant to be a fixed rule: the column runs I, II, 3, IV, IV, 06, VII, 8, 09, X, 11, XII, 13, XIV, mixing Roman, Arabic and zero padded forms, repeating IV twice, and plate XIV has no picture file and plate VII no credit.

The counter card is the closest of the five to its written identity. The ground is a warm off white that reads as Document Paper F4F2EC, the producer name Raymond Hollis is set in a serif in a very dark navy consistent with Ink Navy 1E2A3A, the licence and branch lines sit under it in a grey sans close to Slate 4A5560, and the disclosure returns to the serif at small size. Two Heritage Green 3C6B54 hairline rules carry the layout, one directly under the headshot and one above the disclosure, which is exactly the bracketing move the identity now claims as its signature. Nothing on the page reads as an advertisement, there is no exclamation, no urgency and no colour outside the palette. Three real gaps. The card carries no Aldervale Mutual wordmark or logo anywhere, only the company name buried inside the disclosure sentence, which is odd for an institutional mutual whose whole pitch is the carrier behind the producer. There are no plan figures and no recommended plan marker on the card at all, so the parts of the identity about rate figures and small caps are simply not exercised by the surviving artwork. And the embedded fonts are only Georgia and Arial, not the named serif and sans. The headshots vary far more than the sober institutional tone allows. Headshot 01 is a 3024 by 4032 daylight office portrait in a navy blazer and pale blue shirt, effectively on palette. Headshot 05 is 720 by 960, flat lit against a plain beige wall in a burgundy top, a colour that exists nowhere in the five hex palette, and headshot 13 is smaller again at 675 by 900. Printed side by side at the same size on one card run they will not read as one carrier.

wall_mark.jpg is a hand painted black roundel on warm red brick: an anvil silhouette with an oak sprig crossing the horn, ANVIL & OAK arced above and PROVIDENCE . RI arced below. The painted lettering is a serif, with visible bracketed and slab serifs on the A, N, L and on PROVIDENCE, which contradicts the written identity's claim that heavy condensed grotesque caps are the signature. The mark also spells the name with an ampersand while the brand is written Anvil and Oak. meetcard_press.pdf is not an Anvil and Oak piece at all: it is branded IRONSIDE BARBELL CLUB, with a brass circular barbell emblem and a footer reading Ironside Barbell Club . Spring Meet. Its palette is right for the identity, near black ground with brass rules and cream type, and its structure matches the brief well, a heavy condensed cap name over a brass rule, brass letterspaced labels SQUAT BENCH DEADLIFT and bold lining figures, but every trace of naming belongs to the predecessor club. The quote line is set in an italic serif that appears nowhere in the written type system. Portraits are inconsistent as the brief admits: athlete_portrait_01.jpg is a warm tungsten lit 2:3 studio frame in olive and black that sits squarely on Anvil Black, Iron and Brass, while athlete_portrait_11.jpg is a square, cool green fluorescent phone frame shot in a different room, with a third party apparel logo visible on the sports bra and shorts and a BETTER STRONGER TOGETHER wall poster behind. The same poster and third party barbell branding appear inside the meetcard photograph, so the recovered assets carry another company's marks into the identity.

The palette is honoured almost exactly. mark_draft_2400.png is a near black mark, about 1d2128, on a light neutral about f2f2f3, matching Graphite Black on Titanium White, and rolllabel_2025_PRINT.pdf uses Titanium White ground, Graphite Black type, Steel Grey labels and one thin Guard Bronze hairline as the only accent, which is precisely the one restrained accent against a deep neutral that brand_direction.txt asks for. The mismatch is in the wordmark itself. The draft PNG sets APEXGUARD tight, heavy and unletterspaced under a full width rule, which supports the written claim that tight near mechanical tracking is the signature, but both printed pieces do the opposite: shopcard_photo.jpg and the roll label both set APEXGUARD in widely letterspaced caps at a noticeably lighter weight. Two printed artefacts against one draft file means the identity as written describes the file, not the brand in the field. The shield drawing also disagrees between the two: the draft is a tall double outlined shield with a chevron notched apex, the shop card is a wider single outlined shield with a solid filled arrowhead, so they are not the same emblem redrawn but two different shields. The roll label is otherwise on brief, a plain performance table with right aligned bold values, a ten year warranty line and SKU AG-GE-48 in letterspaced caps, no bursts and no flashes. bay_frame_01.jpg is clean and even, grey concrete, dark grey racking, matte black rolls on kraft cores, no drama and no colour cast, correct for the premium supplier band. Note for production: the four files listed as production identity, apexguard_mark_transparent.svg and .png and apexguard_mark_reversed.svg and .png, are not present in the asset folder on disk.

kilnmore_mark_tile.jpg is a brush drawn cursive script, a flowing lowercase Kilnmore in mid brown on an unglazed clay tile. That is the single clearest contradiction in the set: the written identity calls for a quiet humanist serif for the mark, and brand_notes.txt states nothing script, nothing ornamented, yet the only surviving mark is a script. The tile itself is warm terracotta pink, roughly d8a98a, which is not in the palette at all; the linen it sits on is close to Bench Linen. linesheet_2025_PRINT.pdf then disagrees with the tile: it sets Kilnmore as a letterspaced transitional serif at the head of the page, so the printed collateral and the physical mark are two different brands typographically. The line sheet is otherwise right, Bench Linen cream ground, serif product name, sans spec table with grey labels, a physical glaze chip captioned OATMEAL . MATTE that reads as the real Oatmeal d8c8a9, and prices set as 34 dollars retail beside 17 dollars wholesale with the wholesale figure in a lighter grey and not italic. counter_2024.jpg pulls the other way again: the shop signage is handwritten chalk script, Better Things Ahead and Small studio Big dreams, plus a handwritten card reading Handmade Functional Ceramics for everyday life, all of it in exactly the script register the notes prohibit and in a cheerier voice than the brand writes. The cobalt bowls there read brighter and more saturated than Cobalt Slip 3a4e6b. range_capture_01.jpg is correct in mood, one mug given room on a full frame, but the linen ground is a cool grey rather than the warm Bench Linen cream of the printed sheet, so the photography and the page stock do not currently share a white.

Tone and type are right and the emblem is not. All four pieces sit in Federal Navy on a cream close to Paper White, all four set the firm in a sober serif, and nothing is showy, so the price band and the fiduciary register read correctly. But the compass rose is drawn four different ways. northwind_mark_flat.png has eight needle thin rays crossing a thin outer ring around an open white centre disc, with NORTHWIND over ADVISORY PARTNERS stacked and centred beneath in serif caps. northwind_mark_letterpress_card.jpg has a fatter eight point star inside a solid filled circle with an oval centre, and it is a horizontal lockup, emblem left and type right, not the stacked one. northwind_folder_foil.jpg is a third drawing again, broad radiating triangles with a large solid centre, blocked in gold foil on a board that reads near black charcoal rather than Federal Navy 1e2a3a. adviser_card_2025_press.pdf carries a fourth version, a brass eight point star with no ring at all. Two things on the card are exactly on brief and worth keeping: the short Compass Brass rule under the name, and CFA, CAIA set in brass letterspaced caps and left roman, honouring the rule against italicising a designation, while the sector line Endowments and Foundations is the italic. The card's contact lines are set in a plain grotesque rather than letterspaced caps. northwind_sitting_01.jpg is a correct sober headshot, navy jacket, white shell, even light, but its mid grey backdrop is darker and cooler than Conference Grey c9cbc9. Note for production: northwind_mark_transparent.svg and .png and northwind_mark_reversed.svg and .png, all listed as production identity, are not present in the asset folder on disk.

The inherited look is genuinely consistent with the written identity. keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf is an Archive Cream page close to efe9dc, a single photograph in a hairline grey keyline, a name set in an old style serif with true old style figures, and a footer line reading In memory of Walter Fernwood, then the years, set in small caps. That is the calm serif the brief describes and it supports Adobe Caslon Pro as the text face. The photographs match the palette and the no brightening rule: postcard_marvelli_01_front.jpg is a warm sepia real photo postcard of a stage act with a cabinet, its corners chipped and its edges foxed, all of it left visible; postcard_marvelli_01_back.jpg is warm cream stock with POST CARD in light letterspaced caps, fine copperplate handwriting and an ink blot sitting over the last two words, untouched; colour_1968_porch.jpg is a faded warm colour snapshot, cream clapboard, blue floral cotton and dusty green foliage that sits close to Mount Grey and Muted Sage. Two things do not square. First, the file named as the 2019 press piece carries Walter's own dates, 1930 to 2024, in its footer while naming a different person, Arthur Bell, in the body, so it reads as a mourner card for the 2024 service rather than the 2019 file it is labelled as, and its caption text stops mid sentence after the words every summer for, which looks like a clipped text frame rather than a written line. Second, no sans face appears anywhere on that press file, although the identity specifies a light grotesque for captions, folios and dates, so the caption system has no precedent in the inherited artwork and has to be established rather than matched.

The window photograph shows exactly what the identity describes: a hand painted cream rope oval enclosing a lighthouse with H and R beneath it. The cream paint is a warm ivory sitting very close to #F4ECDD. The letterforms are a signwriter's roman with thin flat serifs and low stroke contrast, and the R is drawn about four fifths the height of the H, a painter's quirk no typeface will reproduce, which supports the rule that the mark is photographed and never retyped. The sign is on weathered grey glazed timber above the harbour, so none of the navy, tan, slate or red appears in this asset; the palette is unevidenced here rather than contradicted. The 2025 press sheet does carry all five colours correctly, cream ground, navy headline and price, a Buoy Red rule under the price, sea slate spec strip and rope tan separators, but it is set in Georgia and Helvetica Neue standing in for Tiempos Headline and Söhne, and the HR mark appears nowhere on the sheet, so the one piece of artwork the brand actually owns is missing from the only piece that shows the brand. One batch level note: this rope ring device is very close to the Cedarline seal rim and to the Halden and Roe roundel, so those three marks are not blind distinguishable from one another.

The seal photograph is a true blind emboss, no ink, on warm cream stock very close to #F3EBD8, with a rope rim circle, a cedar tree and CEDARLINE INSTITUTE plus 1978 in letterspaced inscriptional caps with fine bracketed serifs, which does square with the Trajan Pro claim. The lockup inside the ring is off axis though: CEDARLINE arcs down to the right, INSTITUTE sits below it at a different angle, 1978 lands at lower right instead of centred at the foot, and the tree is pushed left of the ring's centre, so the artwork is not centred within its own rim. The 2019 executive diploma then contradicts the written identity three times over. It is set entirely in Times New Roman rather than Canela Deck, Trajan Pro and Freight Text Pro. The candidate name Eleanor Whitfield runs inline inside the body paragraph at body size instead of standing alone at 42 pt, which destroys the premise that the name is the subject. And the seal printed on it is gold and green rather than blind embossed, with its arc text broken so it reads DARLINE INSTITU and the 1978 half hidden behind the tree. The palette is the part that holds: cream ground, engraved gold double rule border and cedar green caps.

The lectern plate is warm polished brass matching Engraved Brass #A98544, mounted on dark wood under warm downlights, and it reads exactly as heavy, discreet and expensive as the price band asks. The mark is a circle crossed by a vertical meridian with two lens shapes inside. MERIDIAN SUMMIT is engraved in a light geometric sans, all caps, tracked very wide at roughly 0.15 em, which is consistent with the Founders Grotesk tracked caps half of the identity, although the drawn weight is Light rather than Regular and the letterforms are more geometric than a neo grotesque. There is no serif lettering anywhere in the summit's own mark, so GT Sectra Fine is asserted in writing and evidenced nowhere. The 2026 badge is structurally faithful: deep ink navy field at #1B2733, warm stone organisation line at #DED6C7, brass track line at #A98544, paper off white at #F5F2EC, a serif delegate name, tracked sans caps for organisation and track, photo forward, no colour block. Two honest gaps. The print file embeds Georgia and Helvetica Neue as substitutes for GT Sectra Fine and Founders Grotesk. And the track OPERATORS is differentiated by brass colour as well as by spacing, which softens the stated rule that the track is carried as spacing rather than as colour.

The stamp is impressed into a buff stoneware foot whose clay sits between Oatmeal Cream #E6DCC6 and Kraft Tan #B79C74, and it reads HALDEN & ROE arcing clockwise in letterspaced serif caps with fine bracketed serifs around a conjoined HR monogram inside a thin ring. Two concrete problems. The stamp uses an ampersand while the brand name is written Halden and Roe everywhere else, so the mark and the name do not agree. And a pale glaze run has flooded the lower right of the impression and partly buried the final E of ROE, so this photograph cannot serve as clean source artwork for the footer mark without retouching or a second shot. The 2026 catalog page is right in tone, generous margins, one piece to a page, the trade price stated once as 62 dollars with no bold, box or star, and the photograph shows reactive oatmeal breaking pale at the rim and pooling brown in the throwing rings exactly as the copy claims. But it is set entirely in Georgia, so the spec block and the piece code sit in a serif rather than Atlas Grotesk, and the value column in that block is ragged, with CAPACITY, GLAZE, LEAD TIME and CARTON each starting at a different horizontal position.

Three findings, and the last matters most. First, the two artefacts disagree with each other about the wordmark. On the producer card the lockup is a detailed veined oak leaf inside a green shield beside ALDERVALE MUTUAL set on one line in bold sans caps in warm grey over a horizontal rule. On the 2025 renewal card the same lockup is a simplified rounded leaf on a long stem inside the shield beside ALDERVALE MUTUAL stacked on two lines in letterspaced serif caps with a vertical green rule between. Two different leaves, two different faces, two different arrangements, and the identity says this mark is reproduced and never retyped. Second, the identity forbids display and condensed faces and names Chronicle Text and Chronicle Display, yet the producer card wordmark it tells you to reproduce is a bold sans, and the renewal card is set entirely in Georgia. Both artefacts also read ALDERVALE MUTUAL while the brand name is Aldervale Mutual Assurance. Third, the file named aldervale_brand_sheet.pdf is not an Aldervale brand sheet at all. It is a single small page holding a grey placeholder box labelled PIECE IMAGE, the words The Vesper and the code REF 0417, set in Helvetica. It carries none of the guidance the brief attributes to it, no house green, no warm grey, no type families, no clear space diagram and no rule about the mark never sitting on a photograph. It looks like a product piece card belonging to another brand that landed in this folder. The palette is the one thing that holds: the renewal card uses #21473A, #8B8378, #F3EDE1 and #2A2926 exactly, and the producer name is set larger than the offer as required.

The painted banner is on palette and off type. Hung by rope over a farm gate at golden hour with its right third in deep shade, it carries the wordmark arced across the top half in a heavy bracketed slab, Clarendon class, condensed with high waisted proportions, brushed in ochre with green shading and visible amber runs bleeding down under the opening L and the R. Inside sits an oval laurel wreath of two branches meeting at the foot, enclosing a square topped candle lantern with four candles. Canvas cream, ochre and olive read straight onto Weathered Cream, Lantern Amber and Field Green, so the colour holds. The type does not. Farnham is a Fleischmann style Dutch old style with sharp wedge serifs and nothing in any surviving artefact resembles it. The 2025 printed cover, one of only two sources the brief allows fonts to be inferred from, redraws the crest outright as a perfect circle of separate leaf shapes around a hanging paper lantern, which shares neither the oval wreath nor the candle lantern of the banner, and it retypes the arc as live Georgia Bold at 14.84 pt in Laurel Deep, exactly what the brief forbids. That arc is also short of its own words: it reads ANTERNWOOD FOLK FES, with the opening L and the closing T missing. The two printed years then disagree with each other. The 2023 page sets its head in Georgia Bold at 27 pt in Laurel Deep over a Georgia 10 pt body with Helvetica Neue at 10.5 pt, while the 2025 cover sets the wordmark in Georgia Bold at 34 pt and 26 pt in Lantern Amber with Helvetica Neue Bold at 22 pt for the year and Georgia Italic at 15 pt for the tagline. Embedded faces across both are Georgia, Georgia Bold, Georgia Italic, Helvetica Neue and Helvetica Neue Bold. Farnham and Gotham appear nowhere, the biography size is 10 pt against the stated 10.5 pt, and the stated 14 pt sans for set times is absent.

Colour is the one thing that is right. On the 283 by 176 pt label the ground fills #F4F5F5 against Warehouse White #F4F5F6, the text is #1A1B1D against Ink Black #1A1C1E, the rule under the part number is #1B3A5D against Girder Blue #1C3A5E and the spec labels on the companion sheet are #6E7379 against Steel Grey #6E747A. Signal Amber appears on neither piece. Typography is a different story. Every text object on the label is Arial Bold, and no roman weight is embedded in the file at all, so the stated Univers 55 Roman for spec tables, running copy and prices simply does not exist there. On the letter sized sheet the whole spec table is Arial Bold at 7.99 pt in Steel Grey rather than roman 9 pt on 12 pt in black, and both the dealer and list prices are bold. The part number runs 40.34 pt on the label against the stated 36 pt and 85 pt on the sheet against the stated 30 pt, so neither printed piece obeys its own spec. The nameplate wordmark has plainly been reset rather than reproduced: the printed lockup is live Arial Bold, a wide neoclassical grotesque, while every cast plate is a narrow condensed gothic with a spurred G. The four nameplate photographs are also not four views of one plate. The first puts a perspective drawn I beam to the left of GIRDERMARK with ELEVATOR AND ELECTRIC beneath, riveted to a teal green painted machine. The second is an inline outlined GIRDERMARK with a splayed I beam below it inside a keyline border, on a mid grey machine. The third stacks GIRDERMARK, the subline, the I beam and a fourth line reading CAST ALUMINIUM, on a black machine. The fourth sets CAST ALUMINIUM above a keylined inner panel holding the mark, with a second ghost plate visible alongside. That is four different lockups for one house mark, and CAST ALUMINIUM is the British spelling on a Cleveland plate. Girder Blue appears on none of the housings, which photograph teal green, grey and black. Finally, enc_160_component_v4.png is listed for inspection but is absent from the asset folder.

The foil carton kills the central typographic claim. SEVE BOTANICALS is blocked in a high contrast Didone with flat unbracketed hairline serifs, vertical stress and sheared terminals, and a hairline rule runs beneath the whole word. There is not one ball terminal anywhere on it, so the single treatment the identity calls the distinctive SEVE signature, Ogg and its calligraphic ball terminals, is absent from the only surviving artwork of the mark. The card is wrong on tone too: it photographs as a cool neutral greige around #C8C7C0 rather than the warm Bone Card #F6F1E7, the metallic panel across its right third is a copper rose gold rather than Warm Gold #C2A15A, no Deep Botanical green appears on it at all, and the carton is creased through the middle and scuffed across the foil. The serum press file confirms all of this from the inside. The embedded faces are Didot and Helvetica Neue, not Ogg and Whitney. On a 164 by 261 pt label the wordmark is Didot at 9.00 pt in #C2A159, which is Warm Gold to the unit, against the stated 11 pt. The shade name Sable Rose is Didot at 12.49 pt in #21342A, which is Deep Botanical, against the stated 15 pt. The ingredient and may contain block is Helvetica Neue at 4.69 pt in #23201D, which is Charcoal Ink, against the stated 5 pt, and a Soft Sage rule sits under the wordmark. So the palette lands within a unit or two on every hex while every single typeface is a substitute and every size is short. The lot field on a file marked press still carries its unfilled blank, set in a #4A4A44 grey that matches no palette entry. Register is Atelier only, dark green and restrained with generous space, which suits the 48 to 85 dollar counter tier honestly; nothing supplied shows the 6 to 14 dollar Everyday peg tier, so the claim that one mark holds while small and busy is untested by these assets.

The plaque is a cast bronze square on four rusted bolts, fixed to a lichened granite boulder at a trailhead with bare winter woods and a leaf covered path behind it. The seal is an oval holding a heron flying left above a river bend, with RIVERMEADOW TRUST arced across the top in letterspaced capitals and a second arc below, the two separated by raised bullets. Tone and price band are right: quiet, old, institutional in the modest way a four person valley trust should read to households giving 25 to 25,000 dollars, and the heron squares with a palette that names Heron Grey. The letterforms also square with the written identity. They are an old style serif with bracketed serifs, moderate contrast and slightly splayed capitals, entirely compatible with the Adobe Caslon Pro the letter is set in, so mark and body face belong to one family of shapes. Two things do not match. The words are wrong: the lower arc reads PRESERVING NATURAL PLACES FOR ALL TIME, which is generic land trust boilerplate, while the brand's stated tagline is Land held in common, kept for good, and the voice note is explicit that this trust names the field rather than the fund. The only surviving carrier of the mark therefore carries a line the brand does not use. The metal is also off palette. The bronze photographs warm and pink, around #A78E6B across the lit field and #C1966E where low sun strikes the right edge, well away from Bronze Patina #7A6A3F, and the verdigris running down the left side is a cold blue green closer to River Slate #2E4A45 than to anything bronze in the list. Meadow Green and Cream Stock are absent, which is fair enough from one photograph of one object, so this reads as a mark that is right in character and wrong in copy rather than a wholesale mismatch.

The enamel pin is an oval badge on a dark canvas apron, brass rimmed, with a deep maroon brown enamel ring, an ivory centre and a rust orange kettle with a tall arched handle. Colour rings true: the kettle sits around #A35533 against Ember #B4552D, the rim against Kettle Brass #A8823F, the centre against Steam #D8CBB8. Lettering is gold grotesque capitals, widely letterspaced, with EMBERWELL across the top. The lower arc, magnified, reads B, I, R, E, W, H, O, U, S, E. The only surviving artwork of the wordmark is misspelled BIREWHOUSE, and it sets brew house as one word where the brand is Emberwell Brew House. The prior counter card gets the palette exactly right, filling #F4ECDF, #A7813F, #3B2920, #B4542D, #D8CBB8 and #2A2521 against all six entries to within two units, and then breaks the two rules the identity actually states. It retypes the wordmark: the roundel at the head is live Georgia text at 4.93 pt, twenty two glyphs reading EMBERWELL BREW HOUSE, not the pin reproduced as artwork. Its mark is also not the pin at all, drawing a circle where the pin is an oval, setting brew house as two words where the pin sets one, and drawing a squat domed kettle where the pin has a tall gooseneck. Prices break the price rule twice over: they are Arial at 10.00 pt in Ember #B4542D, both larger than the dish names at Georgia 9.49 pt and shouted in the accent colour, standing in a right aligned orange column, where the identity says prices stay roman at description size, never bold and never larger, and the positioning asks for prices set quietly at the end of a line. The faces are Georgia and Arial standing in for Publico Banner and Karbon, the headline is 22 pt against the stated 34 pt, and no italic appears anywhere, so Maple Oat Latte, the seasonal line, is set roman.

The letterpressed compliments card is a deckle edged cotton card on an oak windowsill carrying a fine single weight line drawing of an ornate key with a vine tendril twining through its bow, and CELLAR & CRU beneath in widely letterspaced caps with a hairline rule running under the wordmark. Two things do not square. Those caps are a Didone: vertical stress, fine hairline strokes, flat unbracketed serifs and a swash ampersand. Arnhem Pro, the face the identity names, is a Dutch oldstyle with sturdy bracketed wedge serifs and much lower contrast, so the mark and the written face are different classes of serif. Second, the stock photographs neutral to faintly cool at about DDDED9 and E0E1DB against the stated warm Chalk White F1ECE1, so the card is not the warm cream the palette describes, though north window light explains part of that. The key and the vine are real elements of the mark that the identity never mentions at all. The printed shelf card then diverges further. Its press file sets every element in Georgia and Arial, not Arnhem Pro and Akzidenz-Grotesk Next, and the wine name runs 20 pt where the identity says 17 pt. The key has been redrawn there as a bare circle on a stem with the vine and the wards gone, so the device on the card and the device on the compliments card are not the same drawing. Claret and Brass Key are used correctly, and the price is in the sans and upright at 12 pt, so that rule holds. But the score appears twice, once as a 13 mm disc filled solid in Brass Key with 91 set in the serif and again as 91 Cellar Notes in the footer, and a filled brass disc is the loudest object on a card whose whole rule is that the score stays small. The placed photograph is bottle_shot_11.jpg, a styled interior with a brass lamp and a stack of identifiable published interiors books, which is the fashionable register the price positioning explicitly rejects. The shoot is inconsistent with itself: bottle_shot_01.jpg is exactly right, a Muscadet on a dark oak counter with the racked wall and a chalk list behind it. Note also that les_perrieres_sancerre_v4.png is listed for inspection but is not present in the local assets folder.

The forecourt plate is right on palette and wrong on type. The brushed aluminium field samples about C4C7CC and C7D1D9, which sits on Chrome Silver B7BEC4, and the device ink samples about 4D5458, which is Vanguard Steel 4A5560 rather than Midnight. The device is a pointed shield with a solid dark field carrying a negative chevron and a solid triangle below it, with VANGUARD set clear beneath the shield in a heavy, strongly bracketed Latin serif and MOTORS smaller and letterspaced under that. The identity calls the marque a quiet serif and names Tiempos Headline Semibold. The plate serif is not quiet: it is a chunky display serif with pronounced thick and thin. The category agrees, the register does not. The window card contradicts the identity outright. Every font declaration in its press file is Arial, so there is no serif anywhere on the card and the stated Vanguard signature of a serif marque above a sans price is simply absent. ALDERMAYNE is set in a bold sans at the top. The shield has been rebuilt as a hollow double outline in Chrome Silver, losing both the solid field and the lower triangle, and the wordmark has been moved inside the shield where the V and the D are cut by the shield edge, a lockup the plate never uses. Marque Red 8C2A2E appears nowhere on the card. The photograph is the largest problem. It shows a silver saloon carrying a BMW roundel and kidney grille with a UK plate reading DY67 XHB, while the card calls it a 2019 Aldermayne Corsair SE and the stock feed gives that car's registration as YJ19 KMX, so the picture disagrees with the card's own year and registration and a real identifiable marque is being presented as a fictional one. Behind it another dealer's fascia reads Quality Used Cars, Sales, Part Exchange, Finance, so the shot is not the Vanguard forecourt either. Two rules do survive: the price is in the sans and the finance footer is sentence case. Worth flagging separately that the stock feed's image column holds Windows paths beginning D:\StockPro\Media\Export, which will not resolve at layout time.

The sponsor board matches its own description and contradicts the typography. It is a weathered pale board sampling about B5AF9A to C6C2B8 under the floodlights, carrying the mark in one deep near black ink, exactly the recovery condition the brief states. The mark is a two ring roundel with CONTINENTAL arched over the top on a circular path, CUP straight across the foot, and a conventional black and white football at the centre. Those letters are a heavy condensed gothic with squared terminals, and that is the decisive problem: Druk Wide, the face the identity calls the set signature, is an extremely wide face, so the only surviving artwork of this brand is narrow where the identity is wide. Nobody who knows the board would read a Druk Wide surname as the same identity. The board also carries no year at all, while the brand is Continental Cup 2026. On the printer card the mark has been rebuilt rather than recovered. The two part lockup becomes one continuous ring of type reading CONTINENTAL CUP, 2026, the football becomes a single gold pentagon inside a plain ring, and the whole roundel is reversed to Floodlight Gold and dropped straight over a blown out floodlight in the portrait, so its interior fills with white light blobs and the mark reads as a hole in the image. The card also contradicts itself on the year: the roundel says 2026, the squad CSV gives 2026 for every player, and the set year printed at the foot says 2025. Its press file sets the surname and number in Arial Black and the position and club line in Arial Narrow rather than Druk Wide and Trade Gothic, and Arial Black is not a wide face either, so nothing in the supplied material demonstrates the scoreboard width the identity rests on. Colour is the strong part: Pitch Black ground, Floodlight Gold surname and number, Kit Crimson rule, Steel Rule year and Card White club line all sit at the stated hexes. The exceptions are Deep Field Green 123A2A, which appears nowhere because the pitch in the portrait is bright saturated grass, and the player's shirt, which is a dark maroon rather than Kit Crimson B4232B. Note also that bruno_ferraz_portrait_v4.png is listed for inspection but is not present in the local assets folder.

The gate sign and the printed tags disagree with each other, and the sign is the one that is off. It is a slate plaque bolted with rusted iron straps to a dry stone pier, routed and painted in warm cream, with a single pinnate fern frond above the name. That slate is blue. It samples 1D3245, 192E40 and 283D53 across the shaded field, while the palette's Slate Grey 4A4E48 is a neutral green grey, and the whole rest of the palette is warm and earthy: Fern Green, Bench Cream, Terracotta, Bark Brown, Sage. Only the right hand edge, where a low sun catches it, neutralises to about 3F3F3F. The lettering is a monumental incised Roman capital, letterspaced, with sharp triangular serifs and clear stroke modulation. It is upright, all caps, and contains no italic anywhere, while the written identity makes an italic Latin line the house signature and names Freight Text Pro, a text serif. Carved Roman caps and a text serif are not the same voice. The fern frond is a real part of the mark that the identity never mentions. The photograph is also unusable as a recovery source: a hand and a phone sit in front of the lower left and the initial F is outside the frame, so the wordmark reads ERNCROFT NURSERY and the mark cannot be lifted whole from this image. The two printer files are named the wrong way round against the identity's own size system. The file called benchtag is 148 by 210 mm with the common name at 28 pt, which is the identity's hangtag, and the file called hangtag is 55 by 90 mm with the common name at 15.5 pt, which is close to the identity's 55 by 85 mm department tag. Both are set in Georgia and Arial rather than Freight Text Pro and National 2. The tags are otherwise the consistent part of this set. The italic Latin signature survives and is right in spirit, with Echinacea purpurea directly under Coneflower in serif italic in Fern Green 3E5A34, the common name in Slate Grey 4A4E48 and the care line in Bark Brown 6B4E36, all exactly at the stated hexes on a Bench Cream EFE9DC ground, and the large tag uses a flat Sage 9AA988 panel in place of a photograph, which is on palette and deliberate. Two drifts are worth naming. The price has crept up: the identity puts it at 8 pt against a 15 pt Latin, the small tag runs 9 pt against 10 pt and the large tag 13 pt against 17 pt, so the rule that the price never exceeds the Latin holds but the restraint it exists to protect has thinned. And the photograph on the small tag is a black plastic nursery pot on a weathered bench in harsh midday sun with gravel and a run of identical pots behind, which is the big box rack the price positioning explicitly places itself above. Note also that the three synthetic botanical references listed for inspection are not present in the local assets folder.

These are not the works of a contemporary selling show. 1994-112 and 2016-084 are late nineteenth or early twentieth century tonalist and Impressionist river weir landscapes, one a moonlit nocturne and one a pale dawn, both in dark stained wood frames. 2013-041 is a Byzantine or Italo Cretan Virgin and Child in egg tempera and gold leaf on panel in a carved giltwood frame. The identity is a Philadelphia commercial gallery mounting selling shows of contemporary work, and the press file's own label reads Marisol Enback, The Long Field, 2022, oil and wax on linen. Three of the four supplied works could not carry that label. Only 2023-011 reads contemporary, a torn paper and stitched collage on canvas in red, bone and kraft. The photography runs on two incompatible conventions. The three historic works are shot as a warm tungsten museum hang and their walls sample BB976C, CCAD88 and A88E6B, a deep amber tan, while the palette's Gallery White is F6F4EF and its Warm Grey Ground is D8D3C8. Neither appears anywhere. 2023-011 is the opposite, propped leaning against a cold concrete wall at about 7B848B on a concrete floor in flat daylight, a storage record rather than a hang. Two frames also carry another institution's wall labels: 1994-112 has a printed label at the right edge and 2013-041 has one at lower left whose medium line ends in on Wood above a century date, so the only surviving reference for how a label sits beside a work is somebody else's label system. The gilt frames and an entire gold ground panel put far more gold into the set than the palette's Brass 9C7A3C was ever meant to carry as an accent, and heavy ornate frames read straight against an identity whose whole claim is austerity. The accession numbers themselves span 1994 to 2023, which reads as a permanent collection rather than an autumn show of forty one works by nine artists. Two things in the surviving press file are worth recording alongside this. The artist line is set roman with no small caps and no letterspacing, so the house signature the identity names as its own is absent from the one file kept as the look to keep, and the accession is left in Ink Black rather than Graphite 55565A. The label also carries a placed reproduction of the work 78 by 80 mm on a 105 by 148 mm card, on a label the identity describes as quiet type high on a large card with unprinted stock beneath.

emberoak_mark.png is a tall oval, not the thin ring the brief describes, drawn as a single hairline stroke around EMBER stacked above AND OAK with a small flame glyph standing in for the word and. The letterforms are a very heavy, very condensed sans in the Knockout or Druk register: flat sided bowls, square terminals, no serifs anywhere. That contradicts the written identity, which names a heavy slab serif as the display voice, so nothing in the recovered mark would lead a viewer to a slab. The mark is one flat near black ink on a warm cream that reads close to the stated Cream, but the cream square carries a soft diagonal gradient and a darker corner, confirming it is baked into a picture rather than sitting on a transparent ground, and it holds none of the ember or flame colour. emberoak_hero_pass.jpg and emberoak_broll_01.mov are exactly the written brand: a bone crusted tomahawk on a cream stoneware plate with the oven mouth burning behind it, and a hearth of split oak with flame yellow over charcoal, so Charcoal, Ember Orange, Flame Yellow, Oak Brown and Cream all appear as specified and the frame is appetite first within two seconds. emberoak_hero_safety.jpg is the outlier: the same cut of beef, flat lit on grey stainless in front of a dormant grey stone hearth with only a thin line of coals, cool and even. Nothing in that frame is warm, loud or hearth lit, so it reads as a supplier catalogue photograph rather than the room, and it would carry none of the palette if used.

ironwood_wordmark.png is IRONWOOD stacked over KITCHEN in ultra condensed capitals, but the weight is Light and the strokes are hairlines, the opposite of the Bold neo grotesque the identity says carries everything, and the letters are spaced open rather than the stated minus two percent. It sits on pure white rather than the Bench White in the palette, and the export is cropped so tightly that the I and the final D and N touch or break the frame edge, which will show as a clipped edge anywhere it is placed. ironwood_bowls_01.jpg is right: a cream fibre bowl of brown rice, grilled chicken, black beans, charred corn, pico and a green crema shot square on brushed stainless, holding Bench White, Steel Grey, Salsa Clay and Field Green, with a blank grey card in frame waiting for a name. ironwood_case_03.mp4 is also right, kraft bowls under clear domes in a lit case on white tile with tiny price tickets, though the case light is a cold blue white rather than the warm Bench White. The two problem clips are ironwood_kitchen_02.mp4, which shows a chef in a formal double breasted white jacket with black piping plating salmon and peas into a five compartment catering tray, a different product at a different price band from a twelve dollar counter bowl, and ironwood_counter_05.mp4, which is a warm domestic kitchen in taupe and oak where a hand sets down a lidded ceramic tureen, again not the bowl, not the case and not the palette. Those two read as a caterer and a home cook rather than a working grab and go kitchen.

Only one of the four supplied pieces is actually Halden Greens. halden_creator_still_01.jpg is the real product and it is on identity: a cream tub with a sage lid that matches Mint Lid closely, on light oak against white tile, with HALDEN GREENS set in letterspaced dark capitals over a short green rule, plain and unstyled. halden_wordmark.png is the same words but degraded, a thin geometric capital sans in which individual letters print at different greys, the A and the G near black and the rest mid to light grey, with no green anywhere, so the file carries neither the brand colour nor the green rule that the tub already establishes, and its weight is far lighter than the Buch the identity specifies. halden_tone_reference.png is not this brand at all: it is a phone screenshot of a discovery feed showing a cast iron skillet on a scratched wood board, captioned It just gets better under the line CAST AND COAL Cookware, a different company in a brown and navy palette with nothing green in it. halden_thumb_hero.jpg carries a third party product on camera, a cream tub with a mint lid and a leaf mark reading everwell DAILY COLLAGEN PEPTIDES, with Skin, Hair, Nails and Joints printed on the front, inside a video player chrome titled Healthy Habits, Happier You. The tub colours happen to match the palette, but the name is another brand, the product is collagen rather than greens, and the on pack benefit claim is exactly the sort of promise the compliance rule and the sceptical voice forbid.

sablefinch_mark_scan.png is a fine line finch on a branch beside SABLE AND FINCH in letterspaced capitals, printed in a muted gold very close to Finch Gold on a warm off white close to Shell, so the colour is right. The letterforms, however, are a high contrast Didone with hairline serifs and ball free vertical stress, not the warm text serif the identity names, and the mark uses an ampersand and drops the word Realty while the brand is written Sable and Finch Realty. sablefinch_open_house_card.pdf is the same Didone family on a Shell ground with a Finch Gold rule, gold price and Harbor Slate facts, which is handsome and clearly the same house style, but it breaks two of the written prohibitions outright: OPEN HOUSE, MARBLEHEAD and THE NEIGHBOURHOOD are all set in letterspaced capitals when the identity says nothing sets in capitals, and the price sets in the serif when the identity says the price never does. The tagline also sets in an italic serif that appears nowhere in the type system, and the caption spells neighbourhood in British form on a Massachusetts card. sablefinch_exterior_01.jpg and sablefinch_walkthrough_08.mp4 are exactly on brand, grey shingled gambrel and colonial houses at dusk with white trim, hydrangeas and warm lamplight in the windows, sitting squarely on Harbor Slate, Shell and Finch Gold. sablefinch_look_reference.jpg is the odd one: a warm golden hour living room with a surfboard leaning by the glass and the sun setting over an open Pacific beach, which is West Coast surf, not the east facing North Shore, so its geography contradicts the properties even though its cream and slate tones sit close to the palette.

sterlingrow_lobby_plaque.jpg is a handheld frame of a cast brass plaque on riven near black stone, lit from one warm source, with the photographer's hands reflected in the metal and visible scratches and a drip mark across the face. The colour is right, the brass reads close to Cast Brass against Near Black and Slate, and the tone is correct for the tier, discreet and worn rather than new. The letterforms are raised serif capitals with bracketed serifs and moderate contrast, an engraved transitional face, which sits against the written rule that nothing sets in a serif; the identity reconciles this only because the plaque is reproduced as artwork and never retyped, so the type system and the one surviving wordmark will never share a shape. sterlingrow_residence_still_01.jpg is fully on brand: a full floor loft with exposed brick, black steel factory windows, a city skyline, wide oak boards, a cream sectional and a grey wool rug, quiet, neutral and clearly the stated four million dollar band, though the brick reads a warm red that appears nowhere in the palette. sterlingrow_walkthrough_04.mp4 is below that band: patchily repointed brick, a mixed orange pine floor, a painted board door, a small wire framed coffee table, a plain grey fabric sofa and a white filing cabinet under flat overcast light, which reads as a mid market rental loft rather than one of nine full floor residences. sterlingrow_brand_note.txt is consistent with everything written, and its type instruction, no high contrast display serif and no heavy grotesque, matches the near neutral system.

The certificate is one printed sheet photographed on a warm desk under lamplight. The mark is an open laurel wreath of two branches meeting at the base, not the closed ring the identity describes, with MERIDIAN ACADEMY stacked on two lines inside it and a thin rule both above and below the wordmark rather than a single rule beneath. The ink is the blue grey of Deep Slate #2E3A45, not the near black Ink Charcoal #1C232A the identity names for the crest, and the stock photographs as a cool ivory rather than the warm Cream Stock #F4EFE4, though the lamp accounts for part of that. The letterforms are full capitals of even height in a transitional serif, not the small caps the identity specifies, so anyone rebuilding from this file would produce caps. The certifying line under the wreath is also set in a serif while the identity assigns all body copy to the sans. Tone, price band and quiet adult register all match: no hype, no gloss, a mid market credential rather than a university diploma.

Three type voices across two assets, and none of them is the one written down. The reception sign sets NORVANT in a light weight geometric sans, all capitals, letterspaced very wide at roughly 200 units, beside a rounded double hexagon glyph in slate on a brushed stainless panel with four visible screws, which matches the hexring description exactly. The 2025 launch card then heads the city Minneapolis in a heavy bold slab serif. Neither face is Suisse Int'l Medium and the two assets do not agree with each other. Colour holds up better: the sign glyph and wordmark sit near Slate #33404B, the card ground is a warm paper white near #F6F4EF, and Amber appears exactly once on the card, on the founding customer tier line and its numeral 40, which is the once per piece rule the identity states. One production note: the sign is supplied as a composite inside an iPhone device frame with a specular highlight running across the panel, so the mark cannot be traced cleanly from it. The broll frame is restrained daylit office, cool greys and pale wood, two people reading printed pages with no stock smiles, consistent with the committee price band.

The two supplied marks are not the same mark. sentinelmesh_mark_export.png is a pointed shield filled with a diamond lattice, drawn in a deep navy near Deep Slate #16283A on opaque white, and at full size its contours are visibly stair stepped, which confirms it is a flat raster export and not source art. The trade show banner carries a different silhouette entirely, a rounded globe of curved lattice lines, so the shield and the globe cannot both be the mark. The banner also sets SENTINELMESH in a light, widely tracked capital sans, not Whitney Semibold, above the line SECURE YOUR NETWORK EDGE, which is not the brand tagline Catch the risky moment. Coach it away. The banner navy reads as a warmer indigo than Sentinel Navy #0B1B2B, and Signal Cyan #2FB6C4 appears nowhere on any identity asset. The banner photograph is also rotated ninety degrees in the file. The office footage is bright daylit generic corporate stock, teal tinted partition glass, fluorescent ceilings and a strip of multicoloured framed prints, which reads mid market SaaS rather than a security contract a CISO defends internally. Four files listed as production identity, the transparent and reversed SVG and PNG pairs, are not present on disk.

The bug is a lightning bolt inside a hexagon inside a circle, supplied at 2048 px as pure near black on an opaque white ground. It carries no palette colour at all: no Volt Orange #F26A1B, no Card Charcoal, and no lettering of any kind, so there is nothing in it to check the display type against. Edges are soft and anti aliased rather than crisp vector, the outer circle is interrupted where the hexagon points cross it, and a hairline seam splits the bolt from the hexagon field, all of which will show at large sizes. Because the white is opaque the bug needs a knockout before it can sit on Card Charcoal. The bench footage matches the register well: plain grey wall, white bench, three portable power stations lined up and a presenter plainly about to use them, honest and hands on rather than broadcast gloss. Two cautions. The set is bright and light with no Card Charcoal anywhere to anchor a card, and the hardware itself is grey with strong orange accents sitting very close to Volt Orange, so the brand accent will compete with the product on screen. Four files listed as production identity, the transparent and reversed SVG and PNG pairs, are not present on disk.

The palette is right and the letterforms are not. The mic flag is warm cream foam very close to Foam Cream #EDE4D3 with DAYDRIFT in a warm dark brown close to Deep Room Brown #3A2E26, but the lettering is plainly typeset rather than hand drawn: even capitals in a light, high waisted roman with fine spur serifs, and the two D forms are identical, which a hand would not produce. The colour relationship is inverted against the written identity too, which specifies Foam Cream on Deep Room Brown while both the flag and the card are dark type on a cream ground. The 2025 episode card sets the title Everything we kept in a high contrast transitional serif with very fine hairlines, a different voice again from the flag roman, and its sponsor sentence typesets the show name DAYDRIFT inside the body sans, which the written rule forbids outright. The card photograph, two people at a table with two boom mics in a lamplit book lined room, matches the two chairs promise precisely. The episode footage does not: it shows three people seated on a sofa behind a pine coffee table with no microphone anywhere in frame.

staticfox_patch.jpg is tagged logo_text but carries no lettering whatsoever. It is a fox head embroidered in orange and cream floss on a navy twill backing with a navy merrowed border, photographed on a grey hoodie under a warm table lamp, so no wordmark and no letterform can be recovered from it and nothing in it verifies the written type. The outline colour across both brand artefacts is a deep indigo navy, sampling around 1D1E45 in the mascot render, not Jet Black 101014, which sits awkwardly against the stated hard black outline signature. The mascot in staticfox_scrap_render.png is on palette where it counts: its body orange samples at FF5D1D against Fox Orange FF5A1F, and the headphones carry a violet that reads as a darkened Static Purple. Acid Signal B6FF2E appears nowhere in any supplied asset. staticfox_refs.png is not a STATIC FOX asset at all. It is a browser screenshot of three competitor channels, BLASTZONE, GremlinCore and NOCLIP NIGHTS, whose twelve thumbnails use cyan, magenta, lime and yellow fills in a chunky rounded extra bold with heavy black outline and drop shadow. The outline and shadow convention matches the brand's stated signature, the letterforms and the palette do not, and no fox appears in any of them. Tone and price band are right throughout: loud, saturated, face and moment driven, nothing tasteful or restrained.

nightform_wordmark.png is a 1400 by 400 flat raster, letters measuring about F4F4F4 on a near black field measuring 030303, with hard stair stepped aliasing on every diagonal, which confirms the claim that it is a screen export with no surviving source. Its letterforms contradict the written identity directly. The capitals are narrow and tightly set with effectively zero tracking, the G and H and the T and F nearly touching, so describing them as wide spaced capitals is simply wrong. What is actually there is a squarish condensed grotesque with flat terminals, a narrow rounded rectangle O and a straight legged R. The neutral white and black also sit outside the palette, which specifies the warm Tunnel White E8E4DC and the blue black Asphalt Black 0C0E12. nightform_card_2024.pdf behaves better on colour: its ground samples at exactly E8E4DC and the short rule under the wordmark is Sodium Amber. The card places that same pixelated wordmark as a solid black block on the cream ground rather than knocking the letters out, and it sets Nightfall Drive and the NF 006 format lines in a plain neutral grotesque, centred, with no letterspacing at all, so it demonstrates none of the specified Söhne system. Tone and price band read correctly: quiet, dark, self released, nothing bright or commercial.

emberline_card_template.pdf is precisely on palette. The panel samples at exactly FBF4E7 Fresh Cream, the runtime and dish note at 60A05B against Herb Green 5FA05A, and the numeral roundel and the Emberline bug at E96C49 and E86743 against Ember Coral E8623D. Its type reads correctly for a warm daytime show: the bug is a bold soft slab serif with ball terminals in coral, underscored by a coral rule the width of the word, and the supporting copy is a rounded sans in sentence case. emberline_bug_grab.png shows the same bug but as a noisy video capture, and this is exactly where the two recorded house colours surface. Its cream panel measures F3F4D5, noticeably greener than Fresh Cream, and its coral measures E5755F, pinker and lighter than the card's. The capture is the weaker evidence and the press card should govern. Two continuity problems are visible in the photography. The show is described as built around one host, but the woman in emberline_keyframe_01.jpg is a blonde in a cream knit and the woman on the card is a brunette in a cream linen shirt, two different people in two different kitchen sets. The keyframe window also looks onto a Mediterranean hill town with terracotta roofs and a campanile, which does not read as Providence, Rhode Island. One consequence of the rewritten system should be stated plainly: the surviving bug is a slab serif, so the Optima identity governs titles, endboards and cards while that legacy on air bug remains legacy artwork until it is redrawn.

halden_desk_board.jpg is exactly what the identity describes in colour and material: brush painted capitals in a dark blue charcoal that reads as Board Ink 2B2A33 on a pale limewashed pine board close to Limewashed Pine EDE6D6, hung on twine against a warm cream wall. The letterforms are hand drawn monoline sans capitals with visible brush texture, a wide splayed A and a squarish D bowl. One written description is wrong. The rule beneath the word is not a hairline. It is a heavy brush painted bar, thicker at the centre and tapering at both ends, roughly a tenth of the cap height, so redrawing it at hairline weight is a deliberate reduction and should be named as one. halden_patron_card_2025.pdf matches the palette exactly, its panel sampling at F6F2E9 Warm Paper and the letterspaced web address in a sage close to Window Sage 8B9B82, and its photograph is the same room as halden_still_01.jpg, same window, terracotta pot, candle, guitar and ceramic mug, so the world is consistent. The type is not. The card title is a bold high contrast Scotch style serif with fine hairlines and sharp bracketed serifs, a different register from the humanist Freight Text Pro the identity names, and the supporting lines are a plain neutral grotesque that demonstrates nothing of the specified sans. The painted HALDEN board, the only piece of brand furniture that exists, appears nowhere on the card. One smaller note: in halden_still_01.jpg the view across the street is a row of multi storey brick terraces with bay windows and chimney stacks that reads as a British or European block rather than Portland, Maine. Tone and price band are right: domestic, unhurried, careful, clearly above a phone edit and clearly below a studio.

anvil_oak_patch.jpg delivers what the brief promised: a stitched canvas patch carrying ANVIL & OAK in condensed capitals over STRENGTH in smaller letterspaced condensed capitals, and beside it a compound ring seal with ANVIL AND OAK arced around the top of a double ruled ring, EST 2020 around the bottom and an anvil glyph at the centre. The embroidery is a rust copper thread consistent with Ember Rust A6552F, read under a warm lamp so it lifts toward tan. The bag canvas is an olive khaki around B68858 that is in no part of the six colour palette, nearest to Oak 6B4A2E but lighter and greener. The serious problem is that the two supplied artefacts carry two different wordmarks. On the patch ANVIL & OAK is condensed grotesque capitals, which squares with Trade Gothic Bold Condensed. On anvil_oak_exercise_card_2025.pdf the same words are set in a bold serif, and the movement name Conventional Deadlift is set in a bold high contrast Scotch style serif in title case, which directly contradicts condensed grotesque capitals and is the same serif used on the Halden card, suggesting a shared template rather than a brand decision. The card also spells the name with an ampersand while its own seal spells it AND. The card is otherwise on palette, its ground sampling at exactly F4F2ED Chalk with a rust rule under the muscle line, and backsquat_poster.jpg holds the right register, a whitewashed board wall, black rubber floor, grey plates and an oak plyo box, honest even lighting with no gym drama and nothing clinical, although that wall samples at CBC6C2, cooler and darker than Whitewash Wall EDE8DF. Two further defects worth naming: cue seven on the card is clipped in half at the foot of the text block, and the supplied photography carries visible third party marks, an Under Armour logo on the tee and ROGUE branding on the plates.

balance_card_2025.pdf holds the written palette well. The episode numeral sits in a disc of Soft Amber that reads close to #D9A24E, a thin Sage rule close to #7E8F6E sits under the presenter credit, and the ground is the warm oak and cream of the stated neutrals. Two things do not square. The card sets the episode title in a heavy high contrast serif while the cleared sentence runs in the sans, which is the reverse of the written rule that the cleared sentence stands alone in the serif, and the strapline THE BALANCE BRIEF runs as letterspaced caps in a sage tint. The bigger problem is the footage. balance_still_02.jpg is the same presenter as the card, shot in a warm oak kitchen set with cream jars and a window, exactly the Warm Neutral and Off White world the palette describes. balance_still_05.jpg and balance_still_09.jpg show a different, younger presenter in a cold institutional lab with cobalt blue tube racks, fluorescent strip light, stainless benching and a grey winter window. That is a second face for a brand whose whole positioning rests on one named presenter, it is the clinical register the price positioning explicitly rejects, and the dominant blue appears nowhere in the six stated colours.
