pulsevault_wall_mark.jpg is a genuine hand painted mark, rough white brush caps on warm red brown brick under one floodlight from the left, letterforms uneven with visible brush drag and a drip off the L, shot at an angle so the baseline converges to the right. It is raw in exactly the way the positioning claims, but the photograph carries no Stage Magenta and no Laser Cyan at all, only amber and brick, so nothing in it evidences the stated palette. pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf does evidence the palette: a near black ground close to #0C0C0F, an opens pill in a magenta that reads close to #E0247C, a numeral in a cyan close to #17C6D6 and a time in concrete grey. Its typography contradicts the written system twice. The wordmark is re-typeset as PULSEVAULT in a widely letterspaced clean grotesque rather than used as the recovered painted artwork, and the act line VELOUR RATKING is set in an ordinary bold grotesque rather than a heavy condensed poster cut, and it is too wide for the measure so the final G is clipped by the right trim. pulsevault_last_flyer.png is not artwork at all. It is a screen capture of an Instagram story with the status bar, a redacted handle, a one view counter and the send message field still in frame, and the flyer inside it uses a stock bold condensed face with a black outer glow, centred, over a low resolution red and blue club photo.

velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg matches the written identity closely. It is a chipped wooden box painted a deep green that reads as the stated Back Room Green, marked in one cream ink close to Lamp Cream, carrying the moth over a hanging lamp inside a hairline circle with VELVET HOUR arced across the top in widely letterspaced caps, which is the arc the identity names as its signature. The only divergence is that the arc reads as full caps rather than true small caps. velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf also holds: a green field, the act name in cream in a serif rather than a sans, the tagline in a rose italic close to Dust Rose, the date line in an amber close to Ember Amber, a short amber rule above the name and a Lamp Cream band at the foot carrying the room copy. Two softer notes. The card's serif is a high contrast didone with fine hairlines rather than the warm lamplit book serif the identity describes, and the portrait inside it was lit on a cool grey studio backdrop, which reads studio rather than back room. next_month_act_03.jpg is not a press image but a photograph of a phone screen playing footage of a woman at an upright piano, with the bezel, a front camera and screen glare in frame and heavy sepia cast. next_month_act_04.jpg is a photograph of a curled newsprint halftone of a guitarist and a cellist lying on a wooden table with a specular highlight across it. Both are warm and acoustic in feel and consistent in tone, and both are unusable as supplied.

milepost_guide_2019.pdf carries the palette correctly, with a headline in a green close to #2E6B4F, a rule in an amber close to #E4A11B above the pull quote and a page in the stated Route White. Its type contradicts the written all sans system: the headline is a bold sans but the numbered steps are set in a serif and the pull quote is a serif italic. The step list also overflows, with step five cut off mid sentence at the foot of the text frame, which is a production defect on the one piece a parent actually reads. milepost_road_still_05.jpg is the clearest disagreement. The hanging street sign reads Milepost Driving Academy in a serif with a small white mountain glyph above it, on a dark navy panel, so the real world wordmark is neither Signal Green nor a humanist signage sans. milepost_glyph_sheet.jpg is a photograph of a tablet held in camera mode, with the camera interface, shutter button and battery reading still in frame, showing a cream sheet taped to cardboard carrying roundabout, yield, stop, straight, lane split, right turn, pedestrian and crossroads glyphs drawn in loose black marker, lit by tungsten so the whole sheet sits amber rather than neutral and one corner is smudged with charcoal. milepost_county_sign.jpg is a real diamond roundabout warning in standard highway yellow, noticeably brighter and greener than Caution Amber, against flat overcast grey that does sit close to Sky Grey.

Nothing in the pack shows the FOLD and GRAIN wordmark itself, so the claim that it is Neue Haas Grotesk Display 65 Medium set tight cannot be checked against any supplied artwork. What is supplied is client work, and it does sit inside the studio palette. cobbleway_carton_face.jpg is a kraft mailer whose board reads close to Kraft Tan, printed in a warm near black close to Ink Black, shot flat from above on a scuffed white painted bench with a hard raking shadow crossing the right third, and it carries COBBLEWAY in a narrow high contrast engraved serif inside a thin rule box with PROVISIONS in letterspaced light sans beneath. That mark does not appear on the product actually filmed. cobbleway_grab_07.jpg shows a gable carton whose face reads Buckwheat Pancake Mix in a plain grotesque with a small brown botanical engraving, a side panel of claims and no wordmark at all, on a warm paper white sweep in soft even light at 3840 by 2160. lunara_grab_05.jpg is the opposite treatment and correctly so for the higher price band, a fluted silver bar pendant on black slate with a single hard rectangular softbox reflection at the top of frame, cool and dark, vertical at 2160 by 3840. lunara_bail_stamp.jpg is a macro of the bail stamp, but the frame is rotated ninety degrees and the crescent and letters sit outside the focal plane, so the mark is not legible as supplied.

The carton photograph shows AURELIAN set in full capitals on an arc above a large serif A monogram, with a hairline rule beneath. Those letterforms are a modulated serif with bracketed serifs, not the Suisse Int'l Medium grotesque the identity names, and they are full capitals rather than small caps, so the surviving wordmark contradicts the written face twice over. The board also reads warm greige, about #C7C5BE on the lit face, against a palette whose Clinical White is the cool #F4F6F7. The printed spec card is better behaved on colour: ground exactly #F4F6F7, rule exactly Signal Blue #3E6076, type exactly Graphite #232729. Its type is not: the INCI panel is set in the same grotesque as the headline instead of Söhne Mono, and the price reads 34 with no currency mark. The reference page sits on near white rather than #F4F6F7, its primary button is a mid grey #4B4F54 rather than Graphite, Signal Blue appears nowhere on it, and it prices the serum at $32.00, below the stated $34 to $68 band and absent from the spec card CSV, whose eight prices do run $34 to $68 but in four different formats.

The 2025 dish card sits on exactly House Cream #F4ECDD, sets the dish name in exactly Bread Crust #7A4A24 and rules it with exactly Burnt Butter #B8823A, so the palette is hit to the hex. The type is not. Braised Lamb Shoulder is a transitional serif at a regular weight with marked stroke contrast, nothing like the heavy humanist ink of Freight Text Pro Bold 700, and the description, the allergen line and the 22 in the corner are a neutral grotesque without National 2's squarer bowls. The 22 is at least upright, so the no italic price rule holds, and it sits inside the 16 to 24 band in the spring draft. The card as a whole reads closer to a wine list than a chalkboard, which inverts the stated feel. The picture also fights its own copy: the line promises slow lamb, white beans, salsa verde and good bread, and the photograph is a ciabatta sandwich with pickled red onion and melted cheese, no beans and no salsa verde in sight. The service shots are otherwise right, soft daylight on honey veined marble, burnt butter and sage and crumb reading straight off the palette, real portions and nothing styled to death, though Scrubbed Oak survives only as one small board and polished marble is a dressier surface than the rustic register claims.

The window card sits on exactly Plaster White #F2F1ED and sets both the address and the price in exactly Deep Charcoal #1E2124, so the colour and the restraint are right. It then breaks the one rule the identity states outright: 1,650,000 is set in the serif, in old style figures, directly under the photograph, and the written identity says never set a price in the serif. The heading 9 Ledgewood Road is a generic transitional serif rather than the quiet, built Tiempos Text the identity names, and the specification line is a neutral grotesque that could be Helvetica as easily as Neue Haas Grotesk Text 55 Roman. The address is upright, so that rule does hold. The listing photograph is exactly on brief: cool plaster walls, grey linen, travertine, jute, dry stacked stone and the bay through full height glass, with Bay Grey, Warm Stone and Quiet Sage all present in the room and no trace of retouching.

The gate plate is a rusted iron casting bolted to a lichened limestone pier with the sea behind it, and the monogram is an interlocked V and C inside an oval with a small anchor beneath. Those letters are a heavy, high contrast serif with strongly bracketed serifs, a smith's cut rather than type, but a long way from the low contrast flared Canela the identity names, and the anchor is a real element of the mark that the written identity never mentions. The agent rate card is exact on colour: ground close to Lime Wash, Casa Oliveto in exactly Verranza Blue #24425A, the rule in exactly Cove Water #4C7A8C, the rate line in exactly Ink Charcoal #2A2925, and 720 EUR a night sits inside the stated 520 to 780 band with no gold in the layout. It is the photography that comes apart. A shade sail at roughly #27814D, a saturated emerald nowhere near the muted #6E7355 of Olive Grove, dominates the card image, and in oliveto_living.jpg the same sail throws a visible green cast across the lime plaster and the linen so the room reads mint rather than cream. verranza_terrace.jpg swings the other way into a saturated golden sunset that gilds the ochre wall and the terracotta, which is the marketplace glow the price positioning explicitly rejects in a brand whose rule is no gold. The plate is also dropped onto the card at top right as a rectangular photograph with stone, path and sky still inside the crop, used as though it were finished logo artwork, the card's serif is a plain transitional rather than Canela's flared half serifs, and the phone number wraps onto a second line.

The hoarding monogram is a hand brushed K and V in a near black navy around #061626, with visible brush drag and dry edges, the letterforms a serif with heavy wedge serifs. It reads as genuine sign paint, but the board behind it is a cool pale grey about #C9CAC5, not the warm Bone Paper #EDE7DB the palette names. The lender payment card is exact on colour: ground exactly #EDE7DB, headline and price in exactly Blue Hour #22304A, the Kestrel Home Lending wordmark in exactly Brass #A67C3D, though the rule above the monthly figure is a lighter #BFA276 that reads more gold than brass. The Spindle is one of the four phase one types in the designer notes, 895,000 sits inside the 780 thousand to 1.45 million band, and the prices are set plainly in the serif inside the copy with no starburst and no bold sans, so that rule holds. The real break is the photograph. The notes say what is sold is the evening, blue hour, cold water and warm rooms, and the supplied interior is a flat overcast midday shot with a grey sky, no lamp warmth at all and a television as the focal point. There is also a jurisdiction problem: dollar figures and an NMLS number sit beside a narrowboat on the water and the British terms SVR, APRC and a repossession warning, which cannot all belong to Beckett Wharf in Providence. The estimated monthly line is set with irregular gaps, which matters because the notes forbid respacing the regulated wording.

The 2019 mount card is a warm cream sheet close to Paper White #F5F1E9 with near black warm type, laid out as a true museum label: a small mounted print at left and a wide empty column at right. The title Ada, 1912 is set in a sturdy transitional serif of modest contrast with old style figures, the 9 and the 2 dropping below the baseline, which is consistent with the written Freight Text Pro Book. Two things do not match the written identity. Brattleboro and Ada Hollis are set as ordinary upper and lower case roman, not the small caps at 8 pt the identity specifies, and no plate number in Untitled Sans appears anywhere on the card. Studio card. is set in grey italic, which the rule tolerates only because it is not Ada's name. The scans themselves are honest and on brand: scan 01 is a warm sepia studio card with corner mounts, visible paper tooth and a deckled edge, scan 05 is a neutral to cool 1955 snapshot with a rough white border and corner creases, so the nine scans are not tonally consistent with each other, which is the restoration job rather than a brand fault.

The supplied mark is a gable peak over GABLE & GROVE in widely letterspaced caps of a high contrast serif with very fine hairline serifs and strong thick to thin modulation, with a heavy rule locked under the wordmark. That is a Scotch or engraved letter. It is not GT Sectra Display Medium, whose wedge serifs and lower contrast look nothing like the painted artwork, so the written identity does not describe the mark on file. The three surviving drawings also disagree with each other: mark_flat.png has a thick peak with a chimney, truck_door.jpg has a thin peak with no chimney, and the 2025 project card has a fine doubled chevron. mark_flat.png is a soft low resolution photograph of a printed card on a grey ground rather than artwork, exactly as the brand notes admit. The truck door green samples near #25312D in shade, in the neighbourhood of Grove Green #1E3A2F. On the project card the ground samples near #EEEFE9, a cooler bone than the stated #EDE9E1, the project name is a third serif again, and the scope lines are a neutral grotesque rather than humanist Whitney. The serious problem is photographic: the card hero is a warm golden hour house with lifted glow and saturated lawn, which is the supermarket flyer look the owner explicitly forbids, while the library itself is right, ridge_road_after.jpg being cool, overcast, unsaturated real stone and gravel. Chapin Road files were deliberately not opened, per the homeowners' restriction.

The roundel is a compass rose with N, E, S and W inside a double ring, with MERIDIAN MOTORS running around the lower arc. Its navy samples #374A5B, a lighter and bluer slate than Meridian Navy #1F2A3A, and it sits on an opaque warm off white square near #F2F1EC rather than the cool Showroom White #F6F7F8, with soft raster edges at small size. The lettering around the arc is a light weight geometric sans with wide tracking, so the written claim of Neue Haas Grotesk Display Bold is wrong on weight and on classification alike; nothing in that artwork is bold. The autumn window card is closer to the written identity, with a navy letterspaced wordmark, a Compass Teal rule, ruled fact boxes and a tabular price, but its tagline under the wordmark is set in italic, and the identity says nothing is italic. Photography contradicts the price band twice over: the card hero is a wet amber lit wash bay, and the raw intake frame M2471 is shot in a dim grey concrete bay with cool shadows and a dark ceiling, which is the dark dramatic look the brand calls evasive rather than the even neutral showroom white it requires. Four files listed for inspection, meridian_roundel_transparent.svg and .png and meridian_roundel_reversed.svg and .png, do not exist on disk.

The house mark is a worn brass plate screwed to the slate pass, engraved with a small scallop shell glyph and OSTRA as widely letterspaced roman caps with fine hairline serifs and strong thick to thin, high contrast throughout. That corroborates a Light high contrast display serif and the Subdued Brass #9C8459 in the palette. The dark site reference is the strongest match of all: the ground samples near #070708, even darker than Near Black #0E0E0F, the navigation and the outlined RESERVE button are wide tracked light sans caps in bone, and one plate sits centred in a black bowl with real speculars on the sauce and a great deal of empty ground, exactly the written grammar. The one divergence is the printed menu card, which inverts the scheme: it is dark brown type on a warm bone paper near #E4DCCB rather than Bone type on a near black ground, so the guest card does not look like the room or the site. Within the card the rules hold, the wordmark is tracked wide over a brass hairline, the pairing flight line is brass, course titles are serif and the wine list is sans, and nothing is bold.

The mark is a solid olive leaf glyph with a cut vein, sampling #737242 against Olive #6B7248, beside NORTHGROVE in a tightly fitted bold condensed grotesque sampling #2E2E29 against Charcoal #2E2E2C, printed on warm lookbook paper near #F7F3E7 with visible fibre and the edge of a neighbouring photograph intruding at the left, exactly the lifted page the brief describes. The letterforms are consistent with the written Founders Grotesk Condensed, though they read heavier than Medium. The colour approval card diverges in two ways: its NORTHGROVE header is a normal width bold neo grotesque, not condensed at all, so the claim that the condensed face sets page headers is not what the card actually does, and the leaf is absent from the card entirely. Its palette is right, an off white ground near #F5F2EC with an olive AW slash CAPSULE line. The product photography is honest and correctly placed between fast fashion and heritage, a heather loopback crew flat laid on warm grey paper matching Warm Grey Paper #C9C4BA with no styling and no gloss. Four listed files, northgrove_mark_transparent.svg and .png and northgrove_mark_reversed.svg and .png, are not present on disk. Note that the new display face is normal width, so the recovered vector mark should be redrawn in GT Super Display Bold rather than traced from the condensed original.

First, the three files listed for inspection as lumora_canonical_v4.png, lumora_hand_v4.png and lumora_marble_v4.png do not exist at the given local_path, so I inspected the real carton, bottle and template files instead. The carton wordmark reads LUMORA in full capitals, in a light monoline sans with near circular O and a straight stemmed R, tracked out to roughly 200 units, with a small four point sparkle glyph beneath it. The written identity claims Söhne Kräftig at 600 weight, set lowercase at 40 units, and calls that the one distinctive move. The supplied mark is the opposite on all three counts: caps not lowercase, light not 600, and about five times the stated tracking. The sparkle glyph is nowhere in the identity. The shade card template PDF embeds only Helvetica Neue Regular and Bold. There is no Söhne, no Inter and no Söhne Mono anywhere in the file, and the 24 dollar price is set in gold Helvetica Neue Bold rather than a monospace face, breaking the stated rule that prices are mono. The carton also sets Amber Hour in a third face, a light humanist sans in title case, unrelated to either of the other two. On colour, the bottle shots are good: gold cap, amber oil, clean daylight on marble and window light in hand, sitting close to Amber Hour #C8792E and Brushed Gold #C6A268 and reading bright and daylight neutral as the brief asks. The template page also holds up, cream ground near Soft Cream #F7F0E6 with a Brushed Gold rule. The carton is the problem: its ground is a blush pink with peach coral sweeps and a rose gold foil edge, and no pink exists in the six colour palette. Rosewood #9E5B57 is far deeper and browner. The brand already warns the carton was shot under shop light, but this is a hue and finish difference, not a white balance one. Two data defects in the merge CSV worth flagging: the price column is inconsistently written as $24, 24.00 and 24, and Coral Flash points at shadecard_peach_noon.png, the same picture file as Peach Noon.

The tissue wrap is the only surviving copy of the mark and it contradicts the written identity outright. The wordmark is set KILN MORE, as two words in full capitals, in a light monoline geometric sans with wide even tracking, with an outlined arch device sitting above the join and a short heavy rule beneath the centre of the word. The identity says piece names and the wordmark are GT Sectra Book, described as a broad nib serif carrying handmade warmth. What is printed has no serifs at all and no stroke modulation whatsoever, so the single element meant to carry the brand is the wrong species of letterform. The two files also disagree with each other on the name: the tissue sets it open as KILN MORE, the shelf card sets it closed as KILNMORE. The shelf card PDF embeds only Arial and Georgia. The piece name Tide Mug is Georgia, which is at least a serif and so directionally right, but the glaze name, the dimension line, the body copy and the KILNMORE wordmark at the foot are all Arial, which breaks the card's own stated rule that a piece name never shares a face with the sans and leaves the wordmark in the body sans. There is no GT Sectra and no Untitled Sans in the file. A layout defect too: the KILNMORE wordmark at the foot of the card overlaps the last line of body copy reading stovetop or open flame. Colour is the strong part. The card's header band is Celadon Drift and is labelled #9FB3A2 on the card itself, matching the palette exactly, and the range capture shows a matte celadon mug with a raw clay foot on a plain near white ground in soft even daylight, neutral and airy, true to the stated house look and to the marketplace intake rule about a plain near white ground. The one colour inconsistency is inside the shelf card: the glaze photograph it crops in sits on warm orange brown wood, which is off the neutral airy ground the brand describes and off the plain ground rule in its own house notes.

The mark itself holds up. The bench block engraving shows A&F inside a double keyline oval with a small diamond lozenge below it, and the letterforms are a genuine high contrast serif with fine hairlines, bracketed serifs and a traditional serif ampersand, so the identity's claim of a high contrast serif is honest. The same roundel appears on the provenance card, so the device is consistent across the two artefacts. The nuance is weight: the engraved A&F is a sturdy bookish serif with visible stem mass, not the extreme light editorial face that Canela Light 300 implies, so a reviewer matching the mark to the written spec would find it a shade heavier than described. The printed card is where the system breaks. The provenance card PDF embeds only Georgia, Georgia Italic, Georgia Bold and Arial. There is no Canela and no Suisse Int'l in the file. The card inverts the stated roles: the piece name Vesper Medallion, the specs reading 28 mm dia and 1.4 mm, and the making note are all Georgia, while the sans appears only once, carrying the tracked out SKU AF SP26 002 at the foot. Georgia sets old style figures, so the dimensions on a card that is supposed to be read for its measurements have varying numeral heights, against the tabular figure discipline the identity asks for. Colour is right on the card: warm ivory ground near #EFE7D9, near black ink, the medallion cool grey against a warm grey board, oxidised recesses left dark as the house notes demand. The lifestyle frame is the other problem. boxed_card_in_hand.jpg is lit warm and golden on orange brown wood, and the silver picks up warm reflections, while the house notes insist on cold light and silver sitting cool and true under the north window and the palette is built on Sterling #C7C9CB and North Window Grey #B9BBB8. That frame is warmer than the identity permits. One factual defect in the same photograph: the card copy reads sourced from a local refiner in the UK, while the studio is stated as Providence, Rhode Island, and the body face on that card is again a serif rather than the specified sans.

The task listed no assets to inspect, so I went to the artefacts the brand actually names, the press datasheet and the counter and bench photographs. The datasheet PDF embeds Helvetica Neue Regular and Bold, Arial, and Georgia with Georgia Bold. There is no Neue Haas Grotesk and no IBM Plex Sans in the file. The big part number GM-4120 is Helvetica Neue Bold, large and tightly set, which is directionally honest because Neue Haas Grotesk is the Helvetica revival and the written spec calls for 65 Medium. The spec table is the real contradiction. Everything in it is Georgia: the labels Rated Load, Bore Diameter and Certification in Georgia Bold, and the values 1200 kg, 40 mm, 320 mm, 14.2 kg and EN 81 20 50 in Georgia Regular, which sets old style figures. The identity says spec tables are IBM Plex Sans with tabular lining figures and the slashed zero so that 0 and O never read alike. Georgia does the opposite on every count: proportional old style numerals of varying height with an oval unslashed zero. For a supplier whose whole tagline is that the number and the part agree, and whose buyers order by part number, that is the finding that matters most. The pricing panel repeats it, setting $9,000.00 and $7,200.00 in Georgia Bold old style figures. Colour and tone are otherwise correct. The sheet sits on Sheet White near #F6F6F4 with near black rules, the line drawing in Technical Grey, and Safety Amber #E8A31D used exactly once as a single rule over the pricing box, which is restrained and technical rather than promotional. The footer carries Cleveland, Ohio and the tagline. bench_sessions_01.jpg shows a cast aluminium governor sheave on a brushed steel bench, flat even grey with no blue cast and no spangle, matching the finishes note description of clear anodised as the flat grey one, and matte rather than glossy as the positioning requires. counter_2024.jpg is the trade counter under fluorescent light with grey steel shelving and an open parts catalogue, plain and unstyled, with no brand mark visible anywhere, which is consistent with the statement that no working brand files exist.

The type in both supplied marks is consistent with the written identity. SUMMIT & SABLE is set in bold condensed grotesque capitals, tightly fitted, in both files, which matches the stated Trade Gothic Next Bold Condensed all caps direction closely enough that a reviewer would accept it. The inconsistency is between the two files themselves. In summit_mark_export.png the mountain is an outlined three peak device drawn in a single even stroke, centred above one line of type. On the woven label the mountain is a solid filled silhouette with four peaks, sitting to the upper right and overlapping the type, and the wordmark breaks across two lines. So the two logo files disagree on the device, on its fill and on the lockup, and a designer asked to rebuild the mark would have to choose between them. The export is also exactly what the brand described, a flat screen size raster on a rounded white card against black, with visible compression fringing on the letter edges and no scalable artwork behind it. Colour holds together. The label tape is Trail Sand close to #C9B79A, the printed mark is Sable Charcoal close to #26282B, and the webbing across the label and packshot frames is Recovery Orange, although it reads a touch brighter and purer than the stated #D95E28, which is a burnt rust. summit_ridge_blue_spool.jpg shows a deep denim blue webbing that sits very close to Ridge Blue #2F5D8A, perhaps a shade deeper, photographed flat on a scarred wood bench in a workshop with no styling. summit_bench_packshots_01.jpg is a coiled orange recovery strap on a plain near white ground in flat even daylight with the white box stitch at both eyes clearly visible, which is exactly the honest daylight and visible workmanship the brand asks for and is neither cinematic nor discount loud.

I looked at five consignment photographs. Each slab sits on a different surface under different light: dark walnut in window daylight, a warm wood table under tungsten, a green leather desk pad, cool grey stone, and cream speckled granite. None of them shows the Slate Grey #8A9099 stage or the Paper Neutral #F2F3F4 light stage the palette specifies, and Signal Amber #C8892E appears nowhere on a brand element. The only warm gold in frame is artwork, the Ironclad cover logo and a jersey trim. Two labels do carry a SlabVault Cards wordmark set in a bold humanist sans in title case, with a shield and mountain mark on the GRADEX slab, so the claim that no logo file exists is contradicted by what is already printed on the holders, and that sans wordmark sits awkwardly against the serif display face this identity now specifies. Grader names read GRADEX and APEX in caps as the house note requires, and grades read 9.5 and 9.0, but certification numbers arrive in three different formats, SV00048721, #000732486 and 842639517204, which the mono figure rule will have to reconcile. Tone and price band are right: sober, evidential, nothing flashy.

I looked at the embroidered sleeve patch and the 2025 printer file. The patch is a circular crest on navy: a gold outer ring carrying CONTINENTAL CUP in gold caps on the arc, a silver inner ring around a silver triple chevron, two gold stars and 2026 below. The palette is exactly the written one, Pitch Deep Navy, Cup Gold and Stadium Silver, and the printer file adds Floodlit Black in the stadium portrait and Signal Red on the squad number 8. Typography is where it parts company. The identity names Druk Condensed Super for player names, but EMILE SORENSEN on the printer file is set in a normal width bold neutral grotesque with no condensation at all, in Stadium Silver. The position line MIDFIELDER is set in faux small caps, a full size M followed by widely letterspaced smaller caps, a treatment the written identity never mentions. Cup Gold is correctly held for the masthead and the 2025 year line. Both the patch lettering and the card lettering are sans, so the serif display face specified here is a deliberate break from the surviving artwork rather than a continuation of it.

I looked at the wax seal photograph and the 2025 thank you card. The seal is a deep oxblood impression on a warm cream textured envelope, and that cream sits right on Warm Vellum #EFE7D8 and Soft Cream #F7F1E6. The wax reads a touch deeper than Seal Wax Red #7A2E28 in shadow but matches in the lit areas. The monogram in the wax is an upright conjoined FR in a bracketed old style serif with a long tail on the R. The card is fully on palette: cream ground, a Golden Hour rule at the head, serif body copy, Emma and Tom in Seal Wax Red serif, and the date set in letterspaced sans in a muted Walled Garden Green. Two things do not square. The ampersand in Emma and Tom is upright roman, while the identity says the italic ampersand is the one flourish the studio allows. And the FR monogram in the burgundy disc on the card is italic, so it does not match the upright conjoined letterforms pressed into the wax. Warmth, venue, price band and tone are otherwise exactly right.

I looked at the 2025 badge printer file, the brand notes and one speaker portrait. The badge is on palette: a Cascadia Slate #23303A top band, a Warm Paper #F2EEE7 field, a Signal Copper #B06B3E rule across the foot and the affiliation Aldermoor Robotics in that same copper. The CFS monogram top left is widely letterspaced caps in a light neutral grotesque, quiet and correct for the price band. The name Marguerite Halloran and the role line Founder and CEO are set in bold and regular cuts of a neutral grotesque, which honours the rule that a speaker name is never set in the serif. No serif appears anywhere on the badge, so the display face is unevidenced rather than contradicted. The real conflict is the portrait. The brand notes insist every sitter be photographed on the same quiet Fog Grey to Warm Paper ground, never coloured and never busy, yet the sitter on the badge and speaker portrait 01 of the same woman are both shot against a near black studio ground. That is the gap the finishing work exists to close.

I looked at the deboss card photograph and the speaker card template. The card is a warm bone textured stock lying on pale maple, close to Bone #F4EFE7 and Warm Neutral #E8E1D6, carrying a blind debossed AV in a high contrast serif with fine hairlines and flat thin serifs, the A and the V overlapping so their inner diagonals almost touch. The template is on palette too: a bone lower band, a mid slate studio ground behind the portrait near Studio Slate #4C5560, ink text, and the AV monogram bottom right in Ochre #B98A4B carrying the same overlapping letterforms as the deboss. Two notes. The identity names GT Sectra Display Medium, whose serifs are scalpel cut and asymmetric, but the title Designing the thing before the deck is set in a rounder, sturdier bold serif without those cuts. And the identity assigns talk titles to the sans while the serif carries her name, yet the template does the reverse, setting the talk title in the serif and showing her name nowhere. Palette, restraint and price band are right.

The colour side is genuinely consistent. The glaze tile frame shows six fired tiles reading tan, pale cream, olive, a red brown, a near black brown and a light oat, which sit almost exactly on Kiln Clay, Oat, Sprig Green, Ember and Bench Ink. The nine frame grid reference is warm daylight studio work, speckled stoneware, autumn foliage, raw wood benches, and the studio frame confirms the same oat and olive glazes in real light, so palette and tone match the written warm, unhurried, handmade identity and the mid price band. The motifs page is a photographed sketchbook spread with three thin brown ink drawings, a mug, a leafy sprig and a bottle kiln, on cream paper beside a water brush, exactly the informal state the brand notes describe and with no logo artwork present. The typography on the card template is where it parts company. The product name at the top is set in a heavy Clarendon style slab serif in title case, far bolder and more commercial than the moderate weight inked text serif the identity names, the price sits in that same bold serif although the identity puts prices in the sans at 500 weight, and the lowercase two word name signature never appears on the piece. The card ground is warm oat, which does match Warm Ground.

The brand note restates the five palette hexes exactly as the identity carries them, fixes the near black ground for cut outs, keeps the room hero true colour and confirms the six hundred dollar direct only band, so the written system and the client note agree. The room card sits on limewash cream with a cold, grey skied harbour frame, brick, lime plaster, oak sill, black steel window and a charcoal throw, which is the stated material story, and the rate is set small and quiet well below the room name, honouring the one stated prohibition. The display face is the mismatch. The room name is a high contrast Didone with vertical stress, hairline thins and a long swash tail on the Q, much closer to Playfair Display than to the wedge cut Scotch serif the identity names, and its label line beneath is bold tracked grotesque caps, which does match. The brass key fob is solid warm brass on oak with the initial cut out in a bracketed high contrast serif, and the brass tone matches the palette, but both that frame and the plaster and basin frame are lit warm rather than cold toned, which the client note itself flags as the autumn and winter visits not matching.

The maker's mark photograph is exactly what the brand note claims. It is a raised circular seal struck into a sand cast grey iron bracket, the name arched in bold caps around the top, an anvil silhouette centred, the founding year across the bottom, the edges slightly rounded by the sand texture and the whole thing reading in relief rather than as flat artwork, so there is genuinely no vector to reuse and the heritage and provenance claim holds. The spec card is on foundry sand with a furnace orange rule under the image, an orange tracked reference code, grey grotesque spec lines and plain lining numerals, all matching the stated palette and the rule about numerals. Two things do not square with the written identity. The headline is a light to regular weight transitional serif on a sand panel rather than the heavy 600 weight serif with generous black around it that the identity specifies, so it reads lighter and more editorial than heavy and foundry. The strapline at the foot is tracked caps at a size clearly below the 16 pt floor the identity sets for the specifier contact. The pattern store frame is cool grey daylight over wood and sand rather than a hot dark floor, with furnace orange present only as a small glow at the far end.

The input listed no assets to inspect, so I looked at the printed certificate and two supplied frames. The certificate sits on bone cream with near black text and a single thin brass rule under the wordmark, which matches the palette, and the stacked two line wordmark with wide tracking matches the house habit. Three details contradict the written identity. The wordmark is set in full capitals in a bold high contrast serif, not the small caps the identity specifies. The serial, caliber, dial and regulation lines are set in the serif rather than the grotesque the identity reserves for specifications. The timing paragraph, which the identity says may never be italic and never in the serif, is set in italic serif across three lines, so the one explicit prohibition is broken on the client's own printed piece. Only the foot line is grotesque tracked caps. The product frame and the movement frame are shot on cool neutral grey and a cool neutral near black, silver sunburst dial, polished steel bracelet, blued screws and a gilt balance, so they read precise and quiet and would judge finish honestly, but they do not yet carry the warm single tone the identity claims, and no oxblood or warm near black appears anywhere in what was supplied.

The label and the notes are consistent. The label prints on the house black ground with one orange rule, the product name in widely letterspaced bold grotesque caps, a small orange tracked label above the fitment line, the fitment itself in untracked bold sentence case, and the SKU in tracked grey, which honours both the wide tracked caps habit and the rule against tracking fitment lines. The notes repeat the same five hexes, the dark ground and the hard exclusions. The two logo assets contradict the identity's stated signature outright. On the box sticker and on the shop glass decal the wordmark is a heavy, distinctly condensed grotesque set very tight, letters almost touching, which is the opposite of the wide 120 unit tracked caps the identity calls the brand signature, and the letterforms are narrower and more squared than the Aktiv Grotesk the identity names. The device is a chevron with an angled orange bar through its centre, which the written identity never mentions at all. The box sticker is a die cut badge silhouette with a white keyline, modern rather than vintage but still a badge outline rather than a flat minimal mark. The orange on the glass decal reads lighter and softer, around a mid orange, rather than the specified deeper red orange, partly daylight through glass. Palette otherwise holds: house black box board, gunmetal tools, cool steel and off white.

The brief supplied an empty inspection list, so I opened the brand artefacts in the task folder directly. The photography is genuinely on palette. The flatlay ground measures #E9E1D7 and the boucle throw #BBA997, both within a few points of Oatmeal Glaze #E7DDCB and Soft Clay #C9A98E and sitting at the same warm hue of 30 to 33 degrees. The iron glaze vases in autumn_shoot_04 measure #383028 against Stoneware Charcoal #3B3733, an exact hue match at 30 degrees, although a pair of near black vases on cream is precisely the austere collectible ceramic read the price positioning says the brand is not. The one surviving brand document contradicts the written type system outright. In the press PDF the product name Oatmeal Breakfast Mug is Georgia at 16 pt, not Publico Text at 28 pt; body and captions are Arial at 9.5 pt and 6.5 pt, not Graphik at 8.5 pt; and the price $45 is set in Arial Bold at 12 pt, which breaks the identity's own instruction never to bold a price. Its page ground does fill #F6F1E8, exactly Warm Paper Ground. The phone colour note is unusable as a colour reference: shot at night under tungsten, the indigo throw photographs brown, its brightest weave measuring #5B432E at hue 28 where Indigo Dye #33455E sits at hue 215, with the blue channel lowest in every sample I took, and the oak table reading #B0520B. Nothing in the folder shows Publico or Graphik anywhere.

The founders' brand note prints its chips at exactly #3F6B3A and #2C2A24 on a #F4ECD8 ground, all three exact palette matches, but the note itself disclaims that green, saying the true chip lives on a swatch card that was never sent. That matters because the two packshots are the only surviving record of the house green, and they do not agree with each other or with the palette. The elderflower can measures #60776F at hue 159 and saturation 0.11; the rhubarb can measures #4C5B4F at hue 132 and saturation 0.09; Label Green #3F6B3A is hue 114 at saturation 0.30. Both cans are far greyer and cooler than the written green, and they sit 27 degrees of hue apart from one another. The lettering is wrong too. Both cans carry a high contrast Didone style serif with fine hairlines and sharp serifs, not Recoleta, which is a soft, low contrast, rounded face; the identity calls Recoleta the one distinctive mark of the brand and no supplied asset shows it. The two cans also use different label architectures: the elderflower leads with BOTANICAL SODA and a letterspaced sans claim, centres the flavour and never shows the brand name at all, while the rhubarb leads with a Fennhollow serif lockup, drops the flavour to the base and uses no sans anywhere. Their illustration systems differ as well, a cream monochrome engraving against a full colour naturalistic painting. Both grounds are pure white at #FEFEFE, so Warm Cream Ground appears in no photograph. Finally, the two files listed as synthetic campaign references, fennhollow_elderflower_lifestyle_v4.png and fennhollow_rhubarb_lifestyle_v4.png, are not present at their local paths.

The pass card is exactly on palette, its ground filling #F4F0E8 for Warm Off White and its rule #C7A97A for Oak, but its type is Georgia at 15 pt for the word Verda and Helvetica for everything else, nowhere near GT Alpina Light and Basis Grotesque. Measuring the glyph positions, the wordmark carries only 0.4 pt of extra letterspacing at 15 pt, about 27 thousandths, while the small FOUNDING MEMBER PASS label carries 1.80 pt at 6 pt, about 300 thousandths. So the wide letterspacing the identity calls its quiet signature is on the tiny label and not on the wordmark at all. The supplied logo repeats the problem. It is a 600 by 600 RGB export with no alpha, so it carries a baked white ground and cannot sit over the sage and oak photography without a white box, and its letterforms are a Regular weight bracketed serif close to Georgia, set tight with no letterspacing and filling the canvas edge to edge with roughly eight percent clear space each side. Its ink measures #2B2D33 at hue 225, a cool blue black, where the palette's darkest value Soft Ink #33352E is hue 77, a warm olive black, so the mark is the opposite temperature to the written identity. The studio frame contradicts the brief's central claim: at least six reformers are racked in a row down a narrow room where the owner note asks for one body at a time and no crowding, the ceiling is a commercial suspended grid with cool LED panels, the window is blown to pure white, and 39 percent of the frame carries a warm cast against 13 percent cool, producing exactly the orange the owner rules out, with the right floor at #B06742 and the right wall at #A25221. The upholstery looks sage at a glance but is not: the front pad measures #5F7087 at hue 212, a cool slate blue sitting 122 degrees from Sage #9CA98F at hue 90 and darker at luminance 0.45 against 0.61, and across the whole frame only five pixels in thirty thousand fall in the green band. It reads green only because of the orange surround. Separately, verda_instructor_04.jpg is 825 by 1100 where the other five run 2400 by 3000 and larger.

The alliance mark is on palette and off system. Its rings and compass rose stroke in #2E3A3C, exactly Deep Harbour, and COAST ALLIANCE sets in #5B5F5C, exactly Wet Stone. But the wordmark is live text declared as Georgia with a Times New Roman fallback at weight 300, letterspaced 5 units on 48 px and 7 units on 22 px, roughly 0.10 and 0.32 em. Nothing is outlined, so the mark reflows on any machine without Georgia, and it shows a generic system serif where the identity specifies Newzald Book. The two files that would have solved this, alliance_mark_outlined.svg and alliance_mark_transparent.png, are listed in the brief but are absent from disk. The trail card is likewise exact on colour, its ground filling #E7DDC9 for Wool Cream and its rule #C8894B for Warm October Sun, with Georgia and Arial standing in for Newzald and Atlas Grotesk; to its credit it does honour both stated rules, keeping the member name in the sans at 12 pt and the trail number in Arial Bold at 30 pt. The alliance mark on it is reproduced at 6.1 pt and 2.8 pt, far too small to hold. Its content is off brief, though: it features Tidewrack Gallery, which the board note says closed in February and must not appear in this year's run, and its opening line reads May to September, weekends, which is the summer season the whole campaign exists to avoid. The harbour seafood frame is a 5200 by 1600 stitched panorama with a visible vertical seam running through the sky and the harbour wall near the centre, flat overcast grey throughout with no Warm October Sun anywhere in it, and the building sign reads HARBOUR SEAFOOD ROOM, which is neither the registered name nor The Landing Room that the board note says must always be used in campaign copy. The bakery frame is wrong on both geography and season: prices are in pounds sterling at 3.50, 3.20 and 2.80 for a North American Atlantic coast alliance whose visitors spend dollars, the window shows red brick terraces, the light is bright and summery rather than low and out of season, and the file is 1400 by 1050 against the 3400 by 2267 to 4800 by 3200 of the other member frames.

The employer one pager is the one asset that holds the identity. Its page fills #F3EEE6 for Warm Chalk, its header band #2C3742 for Deep Slate and its accent rule #6E8F7C for Sage Signal, using exactly one accent as the notes require, and it keeps the contact block out of the serif as instructed. Its type is Georgia at 30 pt and Georgia Italic at 15 pt standing in for Lyon Text, with Arial for body standing in for Inter. The bigger problem is the inspection list itself. All eight files are tagged logo_text, but not one is Palewell's wordmark. Northbanks Logistics is a navy and steel blue bold grotesque with an S device, Bramble and Fox Grocers is forest green and terracotta with a serif and a fox and leaf mark. These are third party employer logos, and Palewell owns no logo asset anywhere in the folder. All fourteen are 600 by 600 RGB with baked white grounds and no alpha, so none can be placed on Warm Chalk or Deep Slate without a white box. The site grab is the brand notes' own list of prohibitions rendered as a web page: a template at healthwellnessdirect.com with a beaming stock clinician in a white coat and stethoscope, a saturated blue call to action, flat cool grey and a bold neo grotesque headline where Lyon Text should be, against notes that say never cold, sterile or blue and faces present rather than beaming. The one photograph the brand owns outright is only half right. The clinical lead is calm and present rather than beaming, and her scrubs at #9EA8A5 sit near Sage Signal though greyer and lighter, hue 162 against 145 and saturation 0.05 against 0.13. But the room is a conference hall, not a real care room: the wall behind her measures #C8CECE at hue 180, a cool neutral nowhere near Warm Chalk at hue 37, and the frame carries visible third party branding in a navy Clinical Lead lanyard and badge bearing another organisation's blue and green leaf mark, plus a pull up banner reading Better Health Brighter Futures in that organisation's navy, with delegates and exhibition tables filling the right third.

The palette is honest. Basalt near black, Trail Sand tan and Rust Ridge orange all appear as printed inks, and Pine Shadow shows in the ridgeline stripes. Typography is where the artwork and the written identity part company. On compass_chest the N, E, S and W are a heavy slab serif with obvious bracketed slabs, not a condensed grotesque, and the ring wording is duplicated top and bottom around an ellipse rather than a circle. On the hoodie sample the ring caps CORDWAIN OVERLAND BEND OR are a light weight tracked very wide, while overland_badge sets that same line much heavier and tight, so one line of type exists in two different weights. Only ridgeline_back genuinely reads as Trade Gothic Bold Condensed territory, and it adds a black keyline around rust letters, a fourth treatment the identity never records. The tee is photographed on bright white rather than Bone at EDE7DA. Ridgeline also runs green, rust, charcoal and a keyline together, which is more than the two or three tight inks the price story rests on.

Cream Board and Plate Steel are exactly right. The 1974 cover is a warm cream stock carrying one near black ink, and the 2024 nameplate is brushed stainless. The two records of the company mark do not agree with each other. The 1974 mark is an upright oval holding a stacked R over W, with REDECKER MACHINE WORKS and SHEBOYGAN WISCONSIN arched tightly around it, and those ring caps are set close rather than tracked open 8 percent as the identity claims. The 2024 nameplate carries a circular monogram of three interlocked letters, RMW, with MACHINE WORKS arched inside the circle. Circle against oval, three letters against two. The etched plate fields are genuinely generous in their spacing, so the tracking claim is true of the plate and false of the catalogue. The 1919 casting is slab serif, with clear serifs on FORMED TRUE, on 1919 and on SHEBOYGAN, which contradicts the flat grotesque the identity calls its signature, and the paint there photographs as a light sage olive, visibly lighter and greyer than Works Green at 33564A. The proving stamp coupon is the one artefact that is a plain grotesque, REDECKER PROVED struck around a chevron over bar device.

Not one of the four shows a slab serif. Every piece of ring and banner lettering is a bold sans with plain square stroke ends, so the Sentinel Bold claim is contradicted in all four artefacts I opened. The crest shape is also unsettled. The paper reference crest is an upright oval with no shield inside it, while the embroidered jacket crest is a full circle containing a shield, and it prints 1987 twice, once under the shield and again on a banner reading EST. 1987 below the ring. Colour holds on the paper crest, where Rally Green and Vintage Ochre both read true on a cream ground, but the ice trial sheet is a much brighter grass green with a grey mountain and a cast drop shadow, and carries no ochre and no cream at all. The hillclimb sheet is a single deep green ink with rough brushed edges, a third rendering style again. The set reads as work by several different hands over several years, which the brief admits, but as supplied it does not yet read as one club collection.

The palette is the closest match of the five brands. Kraft stock throughout, Roast Brown on the moth, Ash Green on the pour over illustration and Brick Red on the ridgeline, all landing where the hexes say they should. The window mark is genuinely arched, hand brushed and warm brown, with wedge shaped slab serifs and white highlight strokes cut into the letters, so the sign painter claim is honest. Two things do not hold. There is no painted drop shade on the glass at all, and the identity names that drop shade as the thing that defines the wordmark. The stroke terminals are cut and angular rather than the ball terminals and heavy bracketed slabs of Clarendon, so built on Clarendon URW Bold overstates the resemblance. The three bag illustrations also use three unrelated techniques: fine engraved line work on the moth, flat block print shapes with knocked out white lines on the pour over, and a duotone halftone dot landscape on the ridgeline. None of the three bags carries the wordmark, so nothing visually ties the illustrations back to the window. A green oval roundel holding a pale ash leaf sits at the centre of the window and the written identity never mentions it.

The brochure cover is the only artefact that matches what is written. A small oval holds an interlocking I and V in a high contrast serif with fine bracketed serifs and a palm frond tucked into the counter of the V, stamped very small on a warm stone stock with a great deal of clear space around it, which is the restrained flared serif register the identity describes. It is stamped in metallic gold, and gold is not one of the six palette colours. The installed signage tells a different story. Sign 01 is on brand for colour, a Deep Palm ground with Sand Cream type, and it already uses a vertical hairline divider, but its wording DEEP PALM and ISLA VERDE is a light letterspaced sans rather than Tiempos Text, and the monogram there carries no oval. Sign 03 sets POOL BAR AND SNACKS in a heavy geometric sans, very large and tightly spaced across the plate, loud and high in contrast, which is the opposite of the calm upscale register the brief asks for. Sign 04 is weathered painted timber finger posts with chunky hand painted condensed caps and thick arrows, reading as a budget tropical resort rather than a property at 380 to 650 dollars a night. Neither sign 03 nor sign 04 carries the monogram at all.

The crest photograph supports the palette well. The garment is a true claret very close to #6B1F2E, the shield is a deep navy consistent with #1E2A44, and the ram and shield outline are stitched in an old gold that reads close to #C09A3E. Pitch Green appears nowhere, which is expected on a home shirt. The ring lettering and the 1974 are stitched in a light warm bone nearer Shirt White #F4F2ED than Old Gold, so any assumption that the ring is gold is wrong. The problem is provenance rather than colour. The identity says the ring lettering and the numbering are one founder's hand drawn small caps and digits. What is actually on the shirt is full caps, upright, even in stroke weight and regular in fit, reading much more like set type than like the marker alphabet. The alphabet sheet is convincingly hand made, bold black marker with flared stems and visible marker texture on fresh white paper with a blue grid, but it is incomplete: there is no Q and the O appears twice. The digit sheet is a different object altogether, drawn with a thin fine liner on yellowed, creased paper with a green grid, so tool, stroke weight and paper all differ from the alphabet sheet. Those thin monoline digits also work against the stated requirement that the numbering reduce to a single robust cuttable colour, because at shirt scale those strokes are too fine to cut and weed reliably in flock or heat press. The 1974 on the crest matches neither sheet in style. In short, three different hands are visible where the identity claims one.

The shed photograph is genuine and genuinely difficult. The lettering is white paint on silvered grey timber, sturdy slightly condensed painted caps with chipped flaking edges, and it is a painted grotesque rather than a slab, which is consistent with the instruction never to set the wordmark in Sentinel. As supplied it cannot be traced straight: the wall is shot at a raking angle from the quay, so the W occupies half the frame while the final E is tiny and foreshortened, and a hard diagonal band of low evening sun crosses the upper left. Perspective correction has to happen before any outline work. The photograph also carries no brand colour at all, only white on weathered grey, so Harbour Blue, Rust Red, Hill Ochre and Quay Teal are entirely unrepresented in the supplied wordmark asset. The night card contradicts the identity on three counts. First, the festival wordmark at the head of the card is set as live text in a letterspaced serif, with an em dash in the line, which is exactly what the identity forbids, since the wordmark is supposed to be the traced shed lettering and nothing else. Second, the act name The Fen Larks is set in a high contrast transitional serif with fine bracketed serifs and upper and lower case, not the even slab of Sentinel Black in caps that the identity specifies for act names. Third, the card is entirely one colour, a near black close to Deep Ink #22282B on a kraft oat ground close to Kraft Paper #E4D6BC, with no screen texture, no ink build and no misregistration anywhere. For a festival whose whole stated value is the visible hand pulled look across four inks plus the paper, the format card reads as clean digital typesetting.

The house mark is not really the full colour illustration the brief describes. It is a two tone engraving, a dark slate ink around #2E3A3E on a warm kraft cream around #EFE2C6. The dark is close to Deep Sea Iron #1F2A2E but a shade lighter and greener, and the cream ground is warmer and paler than Bleached Rope #D9CFB8. The real obstacle is tone rather than colour count. The rope border, the sail hatching and the stippled sand are continuous tone engraving, none of which will hold as one flat ink at a 22 pt wordmark scale, and the file carries a baked in paper texture so there is no transparency to drop onto a label. Typographically the mark helps the case for the new specification: COBLE & VANE arches in widely letterspaced caps in a high contrast serif with fine sharp serifs, which is closer to Mercury Display than it ever was to the softer wedge serifs of Canela Deck, while the tracking and caps behaviour already match the written rule. The wax seal photograph is a deep oxblood maroon consistent with Oxblood Wax #5A1F1B, although very warm tungsten light pushes it redder. Two things sit against the identity there. The wax is high gloss with strong specular highlights while the brand insists on nothing shiny, and the seal is completely unstamped, so it carries no mark and no emboss despite the claim that finish, emboss and wax are what carry the value. The amber lighting also works against a tagline built on cold light. On the cask label sheet the ground is a warm oat around #DED5C2, slightly warmer than Bleached Rope, the text is a dark teal charcoal consistent with Deep Sea Iron, and the rule under the wordmark is a rust that is lighter and brighter than Oxblood Wax. Most tellingly the house mark is dropped onto the sheet as a visible rectangular cream tile against the oat ground rather than knocked out, which confirms in one glance that no transparent or single ink version is in circulation. The CASK NO., STRENGTH, OUTTURN and BOTTLED labels are letterspaced caps in a humanist sans consistent with National 2 and the figures are lining and appear tabular, but the 58.2% inside the roundel is set in the serif rather than in National 2 Medium as the identity requires.

All three marks are soft raster with a heavy outer glow and not one crisp edge between them. The master mark is an interlocking angular square spiral rotated 45 degrees with mitred corners, an indigo to violet gradient and a purple bloom, on a transparent background. The relay mark is a chevron arrow built with fully rounded caps and rounded joins, a blue bloom, also transparent. The dispatch mark is a circular ring with a breakout arrow that sits on an opaque warm cream rounded rectangle plate carrying a visible drop shadow. They are not a family in any sense: corner treatment differs, mitred against rounded; container differs, none against a plate; glow colour differs, violet against blue; and background differs, transparent against opaque. The account of three separate generations on separate nights is confirmed by looking at them. On palette the gradients do travel between something close to Grid Indigo #2B2E6B and Signal Violet #6C4BD8, so the hues are broadly right, but the dispatch plate is a warm cream near #EFEDE6 which is clearly warmer than Paper White #F6F7FA, and neither Slate Ink nor Cool Steel appears anywhere. The deeper mismatch is with the written identity rather than the hexes. It asks for precise, plain, restrained, geometry over decoration, engineering credibility and never marketing spend, and a blurred neon bloom on a gradient is the opposite of all of that, which is also exactly why the printer and the app store listing refused the files. The booth QR is the only crisp asset, hard edged and correctly quiet zoned, but it is pure black on pure white rather than Slate Ink on Paper White, so even the one usable file sits off palette.

The tone and the price band hold completely. These are convincingly hand painted panels with brush drag, primer tooth and visible bristle marks, unfussy and earthy but not cheap, and the 1 Shot lettering enamel tin and the aubergine sign paint jar on the bench are consistent with the sign painter story. Four of the five palette colours are confirmed in the paint itself: panel 01 gives a ring and lettering close to Cedar Bark #6B4A2E on a ground close to Bone Primer #E7E0D0 with foliage close to Sage Field #7C8A5F, panel 02 letters in a black consistent with Bench Black #1A1714, and panel 03 is stained in a deep aubergine consistent with #3B2B3A. The mismatches are structural. Panel 05 paints its wheat in a warm golden ochre that is not in the five colour palette at all, which is a sixth ink for a decorator working to a fixed ink book. Panel 04 sits on a cooler greyish green primer that is visibly greener than the bone of panels 01, 02 and 05, and it was shot at night under warm tungsten while those three were shot by a window in cool daylight, so the stated two visits under mixed light are confirmed and the panel grounds are not colour consistent between them. The panels are also not one crest system. Panel 01 is a square double ring, panel 02 is a portrait with no frame and a shallow arc, panel 03 is a dark ground with a ribbon banner, panel 04 is a landscape with a flat baseline, and panel 05 is a square with an outer cedar ring plus an inner sage ring. Five panels carry five different lettering styles: a painted Clarendon slab, a condensed spurred Egyptian, a light letterspaced serif, a Tuscan western slab with flared stems, and a heavier serif on panel 05. Even the two ring crests differ in construction, since panel 01 runs its bottom arc clockwise so PROVISIONS reads inverted up the right side while panel 05 sets EVERGREEN conventionally along the bottom. Panel 03 is the one real production problem: its artwork is painted tone on tone in a lighter aubergine over the dark aubergine ground, so contrast is far too low to separate or trap on the same basis as the bone primer panels.

The apron photograph shows a circular roundel: a cedar sprig across the top, CEDAR COMMONS arched on the lower curve and FARMERS MARKET arched beneath it in smaller, widely letterspaced caps. The letterforms are a moderately contrasted bracketed serif with fine hairlines and pointed serifs, not a slab at all, so the written claim of Archer Bold caps tightly tracked does not describe what is on the cloth, and neither does a Bodoni Egyptian slab. It prints in one ink sampled at #2A3028, a near black green that is Cedar Ink #23301F rather than Meadow Green #3F7D44, on oatmeal canvas sampled at #E2D7CB rather than Sign White #FBFAF5. Barn Red and Harvest Gold appear nowhere on it. The garment itself reads as a folded tote with carry straps, not an apron as the brief states. The blank white coroplast sign on its wire H stake in a wet gravel lot under overcast sky confirms the cheap outdoor price band exactly and carries no type. The site entrance photograph is the odd one: it shows a park sign reading Riverview Municipal Park, Parks and Recreation, City of Maplewood, a different park and a different city from Burlington Vermont, set in title case serif with a tree icon on bottle green.

Palette, tone and price band all read correctly, but the five artefacts disagree with each other and partly with the written type. The eagle is an American traditional tattoo bird with halftone dot shading through the wings, black linework, a red beak and a red and black bolt through the talons, on a bone ground sampled at #EBE8D9 against Bone #EDE7DA. The union stripe lockup sits on solid black sampled at #101212 against Union Black #141414, with STATIC UNION set in Slate grey inside the bar between slate and black rules, a low contrast grey on black that will close up at patch size and carries the same dot screen. The arc badge is a vertical oval rather than a circle and runs the two words together with no word space, so it reads STATICUNION, in heavy condensed grotesque caps that do support the display claim. The bolt icon is an outlined hollow bolt in brick red with a needle fine tapered tip, while the badge and the woven label both carry a solid bolt of a different proportion. The woven label sets STATIC UNION in light, widely letterspaced caps inside a true circle, which is neither the heavy condensed grotesque the identity names nor the badge geometry. Rail Gold #C79A3B appears on nothing.

The three survivors disagree about both the house colour and the house face, exactly as the brief feared. The 2019 export sets MAISON SERAULT in high contrast Didone caps, ink sampled at #102224 which sits close to Serault Ink #1B2A2E, on a ground sampled at #F0EBE5 close to Card Cream #EFE9DC, but it is tracked at roughly 0.03 em, nowhere near the 0.18 em the identity claims, and the weight reads Regular rather than Light. The boutique wall carries dimensional letters in a dull antique brass sampled at #856B4A, browner and darker than Warm Brass #B08D4C, on warm plaster under a single warm spot, and those letterforms are a lower contrast inscriptional serif with flared stems, a different face from the export, set far wider than it. The enclosure card is foil blocked in bright mirror silver, a colour that appears nowhere in the five swatch palette, carrying an interlocked S and M swash Didone monogram on ivory stock sampled at #DDD7CA, warmer and deeper than Card Cream. What does hold across all three is the tone: a small mark on a large quiet field, generous emptiness, no logo noise, correctly read as an independent fine jewellery house in the 600 to 4,000 dollar band.

Del's sheet is real and it is plainly the club. Hand drawn humanist sans caps and numerals, no serifs and a slightly modulated stroke, inked in near black navy sampled at #090B16 on aged drafting paper sampled at #D5D5D0, one ink, plain and unpretentious as written. Two problems for anyone tracing it exactly as the brief demands. The numeral row reads 0 1 2 3 4 4 5 6 7 8 9, with the four drawn twice, and the inked alphabet restarts with a second M and V at the head of the third line while the pencil rough beneath runs out of order and incomplete, so a faithful trace will hit doubled and missing glyphs. The singlet badge is a different hand altogether: IRONWAY RUN CLUB arched around a chevron inside a double circle, with a rule, PROVIDENCE and EST 1994 below, all in a clean, evenly spaced digital grotesque rather than Del's lettering, printed navy sampled at #0B1D3A on a pale blue heather garment sampled at #CADEE9 that matches no swatch in the four colour palette. The kit swatch squares better, a deep navy mesh at #18223B against Rail Navy #1F2A44 with an orange chip that reads very close to Marshal Orange #D46A1E.

The plaque supports the identity and the letterhead contradicts it. The weathered brass entry plaque, bevelled and speckled with verdigris on limestone, engraves THE MARCHFIELD EXCHANGE in high contrast caps with fine hairlines and crisp bracketed serifs, a Scotch reading that Scotch Modern matches well, above a laurel wreath enclosing an outlined keystone shield and a ribbon reading MCMXI, correct for 1911. Lit brass samples at #F1CB84, far lighter and yellower than Marchfield Brass #A9863F, which only describes the shadowed areas. The scanned 1950s letterhead sets the same building name in a heavy bold condensed sans with the address beneath in condensed caps, flatly against the Scotch serif claim, and draws the crest with a solid black keystone, a heavy crossing bar and a filled ribbon where the plaque uses open line only. Its paper samples at #FEF9E1, a warm ivory rather than Limestone #D8CFBE, and Oxblood #5E2A2A appears on nothing. The letterhead address reads 42 Lower High Street, Marchfield, Sussex, which is England, while the brief places the building in Portland Maine, and the facade photograph reinforces that: an English stone doorcase with Corinthian pilasters, rosettes, sash windows and lichen, not a 1911 American commercial frontage. The limestone in that photograph does sit close to Limestone #D8CFBE.
